- Omitted or rescued direct array elements retain their positions as `null`.
- A missing or empty list header means “no filter”, which differs from an empty list.

<Callout type="warning" title="Always wins">
`Always(...)` is sent even when a partial reload does not ask for it. Use it for props the page cannot render without; do not use it for expensive data.
</Callout>

## What the client keeps

A reloaded prop replaces the client's value by default. A prop resolved from a loader is sent in full. To combine values instead, use [merge props](/docs/merging-props).

## Deferred and once props

Deferred props are loaded through partial reloads. `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` asks for the deferred group, and the server records which deferred props it has sent.

Once props that the reload asks for always resolve. The client sends `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props` with the keys it already holds, so the server can skip them while keeping the `onceProps` metadata.

## Testing partial reloads

`Inertia.Net.Testing` replays the request with the right headers:

```csharp
var page = await (await client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

var only = await page.ReloadOnlyAsync(client, "users");
var except = await page.ReloadExceptAsync(client, "permissions");
var deferred = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(client, "sidebar");
```

`ReloadOnlyAsync` asserts that the requested prop is present; `ReloadExceptAsync` asserts that it is missing.

---

# Deferred props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/deferred-props

> Load slow page sections after the first render, in groups.

`Defer` leaves a prop out of the first response and lists it under `deferredProps`. The client requests each group with a partial reload as soon as the page is mounted. The page becomes interactive without waiting for the slow data. A deferred prop can also be [live](/docs/live-props): it is fetched again whenever its event is broadcast.

```csharp
return Render("Dashboard", new InertiaProps
{
    ["user"] = user,
    ["stats"] = Defer(ct => reports.StatsAsync(ct)),
    ["chart"] = Defer(ct => reports.ChartAsync(ct), group: "charts"),
    ["activity"] = Defer(ct => reports.ActivityAsync(ct), group: "charts"),
});
```

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "user": { "name": "Ada" } },
  "deferredProps": {
    "default": ["stats"],
    "charts": ["chart", "activity"]
  }
}
```

Props in the same group load in one request. Different groups load in parallel requests. `deferredProps` is only produced on non-partial renders.

## The client

```tsx
import { Deferred } from '@inertiajs/react'

<Deferred data="stats" fallback={<Spinner />}>
  <Stats />
</Deferred>
```

Vue uses `<Deferred data="stats">` from `@inertiajs/vue3`; Svelte uses the matching component from `@inertiajs/svelte`.

## Combining with other props

A deferred prop can also be merged, once or rescued:

```csharp
["posts"] = Defer(ct => db.Posts.Page(1).ToListAsync(ct)).Merge(),
["plans"] = Defer(ct => plans.AllAsync(ct)).Once(),
["recommendations"] = Defer(ct => recs.GetAsync(ct)).Rescue(),
```

The metadata combines: `deferredProps` lists the group, `mergeProps` lists the path, and `onceProps` records the key.

## Deferred scroll props

A deferred `Scroll(...)` prop reports `"posts.data"` just like a resolved one. This is a deliberate fix of an inertia-laravel quirk:

```csharp
["posts"] = Scroll(page, wrapper: "data").Defer(),
```

## Testing

```csharp
var page = await (await client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

new AssertableInertia(page).HasDeferred("sidebar", "stats").Missing("stats");

var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(client, "sidebar");
new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("stats");
```

See [Testing](/docs/testing) for the full assertion API.

<Callout type="tip" title="Use deferred props for below-the-fold data">
Deferred props are for data the page can render without. If the page cannot be meaningful until the data arrives, a normal prop is simpler.
</Callout>

---

# Merging props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/merging-props

> Append, prepend, deep merge and match items instead of replacing the client's value.

By default a reloaded prop replaces the client's value. Merge props tell the client to combine them. This is how pagination, chat messages and incremental lists work.

| C\# | Metadata | Client behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `Merge(v)` | `mergeProps: ["key"]` | Append to the existing array |
| `Prop(...).Prepend()` | `prependProps: ["key"]` | Prepend |
| `Merge(v).Append("path")` | `mergeProps: ["key.path"]` | Append at a nested path |
| `Prop(...).Prepend("path")` | `prependProps: ["key.path"]` | Prepend at a nested path |
| `DeepMerge(v)` | `deepMergeProps: ["key"]` | Deep merge objects and arrays |
| `.MatchOn("id")` | `matchPropsOn: ["key.id"]` | Replace items with the same `id` instead of duplicating them |
| `.Append("path", matchOn: "id")` | `matchPropsOn: ["key.path.id"]` | The match key is relative to the nested path |

```csharp
["posts"] = Merge(ct => db.Posts.Page(page).ToListAsync(ct)).MatchOn("id"),
```

```json
{
  "mergeProps": ["posts"],
  "matchPropsOn": ["posts.id"]
}
```

## Nested paths

```csharp
["chat"] = Merge(chat).Append("messages", matchOn: "id"),
["notifications"] = Prop(() => next).Prepend("items"),
["settings"] = DeepMerge(settings),
```

```json
{
  "mergeProps": ["chat.messages", "notifications.items"],
  "deepMergeProps": ["settings"],
  "matchPropsOn": ["chat.messages.id"]
}
```

The path before the wrapper stays on the client; only the value below the path is merged.

## Resetting a merge

The client can ask for a fresh value instead of a merge by listing the path in `X-Inertia-Reset`:

```tsx
router.reload({ only: ['posts'], reset: ['posts'] })
```

Metadata is skipped for paths in the reset list, and on partial reloads for paths the reload did not ask for.

## Match on a stable key

`.MatchOn("id")` replaces an item with the same key instead of appending a duplicate. Use a stable, unique key from your data. Without it, incremental updates append every item again.

```csharp
["messages"] = Merge(page.Items).MatchOn("id"),
```

## Deep merge

`DeepMerge` recursively combines objects. Arrays are merged by index; use `MatchOn` when you need item identity.

```csharp
["filters"] = DeepMerge(new { search, tags }),
```

<Callout type="info" title="Merge metadata and partial reloads">
On a partial reload, merge metadata is only emitted for paths the reload asked for. `Always` still applies independently.
</Callout>

---

# Once props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/once-props

> Remember expensive values on the client and skip them on later visits.

Once props are expensive values that rarely change. The client remembers them across visits and tells the server which keys it holds with `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props`.

```csharp
["countries"] = Once(ct => db.CountriesAsync(ct)),                                  // key = the prop path
["plans"]     = Once(ct => db.PlansAsync(ct)).As("billing-plans"),                   // custom key
["rates"]     = Once(ct => fx.RatesAsync(ct)).Until(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)),       // client expires it
["tax"]       = Once(ct => db.TaxAsync(ct)).Fresh(),                                 // always re-send
["flags"]     = Prop(ct => db.FlagsAsync(ct)).Once(key: "flags", until: TimeSpan.FromHours(1)),
```

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "countries": [ { "code": "US" } ] },
  "onceProps": {
    "countries": { "prop": "countries", "expiresAt": null },
    "billing-plans": { "prop": "plans", "expiresAt": 1760000000000 }
  }
}
```

## Behavior

- The value is left out on later visits, but the `onceProps` entry stays so the client keeps its copy.
- `.Fresh()` sends the value even when the client has it.
- Partial reloads always resolve once props that the reload asks for.
- Expiry is computed from the registered `TimeProvider`, so tests can use `FakeTimeProvider`.
- `.As(key)` and `.Until(ttl)` imply once.
- Sharing a key between pages lets the client reuse one value across them.

## Keys

The default key is the prop path. Use `.As("billing-plans")` when the same value is exposed under different names, or when you want a stable key across page changes.

```csharp
["plans"] = Once(ct => plans.AllAsync(ct)).As("billing-plans"),
```

<Callout type="warning" title="A key is a value identity">
Two props that share a key are treated as the same client value. Only share a key when the values are actually the same. When in doubt, use the default prop path.
</Callout>

## Expiry

`.Until(TimeSpan)` sets `expiresAt` in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The client stops treating the key as loaded after that time and requests the value again. The server leaves the value out only when the client lists the key in `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props`.

## Shared once props

```csharp
o.Share("plans", Once(() => plans.All()));
```

This is the equivalent of Laravel's `shareOnce`: the client keeps the value across visits.

## Testing

`InertiaPage.OnceProps` exposes the metadata:

```csharp
var page = await (await client.InertiaGetAsync("/billing")).GetInertiaPageAsync();
Assert.True(page.OnceProps.ContainsKey("billing-plans"));
```

Revisit the page with the same client and assert that the prop is missing while `onceProps` remains.

---

# Infinite scroll

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/infinite-scroll

> Merge pages of items and report paging metadata to the InfiniteScroll client component.

Use infinite scroll when a reader should see more items as they reach the end of a list. `Scroll(...)` merges the items inside a value (the *wrapper*, `"data"` by default) and reports paging metadata to the `<InfiniteScroll>` client component.

```csharp
app.MapGet("/feed", (PageRequest request) => Render("Feed", new InertiaProps
{
    ["posts"] = Scroll(Pagination.Paginate(AppState.Posts, request)),
}));
```

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "posts": { "data": [ { "id": 21 } ] } },
  "mergeProps": ["posts.data"],
  "scrollProps": {
    "posts": { "pageName": "page", "previousPage": 1, "nextPage": 3, "currentPage": 2, "reset": false }
  }
}
```

See [Pagination](/docs/pagination) for numbered and cursor pages, query binding and data-source delegates.

## The client

```tsx
import { InfiniteScroll } from '@inertiajs/react'

<InfiniteScroll data="posts">
  {posts.data.map((post) => <Post key={post.id} post={post} />)}
</InfiniteScroll>
```

## Metadata

`ScrollMetadata(PageName, PreviousPage, NextPage, CurrentPage)` is a record. Page values can be `int`, `long`, `string` or `null` (cursor paging uses strings).

Metadata comes from the `metadata:` argument, or from the value if it implements `IProvidesScrollMetadata`. Without either, the render throws with a message naming the prop.

```csharp
["posts"] = Scroll(page, wrapper: "data", metadata: ScrollMetadata.FromPage(2, hasMore: true)),
```

The client sends `X-Inertia-Infinite-Scroll-Merge-Intent: prepend` when scrolling up. The wrapper is then reported under `prependProps` instead of `mergeProps`.

`scrollProps[path].reset` is true when the request lists the path in `X-Inertia-Reset`.

## Combining with other props

`Scroll(...)` accepts the five loader shapes, and `.Defer()`, `.Once()` and `.Rescue()` combine with it:

```csharp
["posts"] = Scroll(ct => feed.PageAsync(1, ct)).Defer(),
```

A deferred scroll prop reports `"posts.data"` just like a resolved one. This is a deliberate fix of an inertia-laravel quirk.

<Callout type="tip" title="Keep pages small">
Infinite scroll is also a payload-size tool. Load 10 to 20 items per page instead of sending an unbounded list on the first request.
</Callout>

---

# Pagination

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/pagination

> Create numbered and cursor pages for pagers and infinite scroll.

A long list is easier to browse when the server sends a small group of items at a time. A numbered page lets readers choose a page; a cursor page uses a marker to fetch the next or previous group. Start with a list already in memory:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia();
var app = builder.Build();
app.UseInertia();

// posts is an IReadOnlyList<PostDto> in a stable order.
app.MapGet("/posts", (PageRequest request) => Render("Posts/Index", new InertiaProps
{
    ["posts"] = Pagination.Paginate(posts, request),
}));
```

Visiting `/posts?page=2&perPage=5` returns the second group in `posts.data`. The default page size is 20 and the maximum is 100; configure both in [Pagination options](/docs/configuration#opagination-paginationoptions). For infinite scroll, wrap that value in `Scroll(...)` and render it with `InfiniteScroll` as shown in [Infinite scroll](/docs/infinite-scroll).

`Pagination` creates page values; `Scroll` adds infinite-scroll metadata and merging. Use a page directly for a classic pager.

| You write | You get |
|---|---|
| `Pagination.Paginate(posts, request)` | A numbered `Page<T>` for a pager |
| `Scroll(Pagination.Paginate(posts, request))` | Numbered infinite scroll |
| `Scroll(await Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, key, fetch, ct: ct))` | Cursor-based infinite scroll using your data source |
| `Scroll(ct => Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, fetch, ct: ct)).Defer()` | A deferred page; other prop modifiers also work |

Minimal API handlers can take `PageRequest` or `CursorRequest` directly, as in [Infinite scroll](/docs/infinite-scroll). MVC and FastEndpoints can call `PageRequest.From(Request.Query)` and `CursorRequest.From(HttpContext)`. Page numbers below 1 become 1; invalid page sizes use the default and sizes above the maximum are clamped. Set defaults and parameter names with `o.Pagination` in `AddInertia`. `From` and `BindAsync` retain the query parameter name for the returned page. An explicit paginator name overrides it.

`Pagination.Paginate` slices an already materialized `IReadOnlyList<T>`. For a database, search SDK or HTTP API, `Pagination.PaginateAsync` accepts a `fetch(skip, take, ct)` delegate and an optional count delegate. It requests one extra item to determine `hasMore`; without a count, `total` and `lastPage` are null. Delegate offsets above `int.MaxValue` return an empty page without calling `fetch`; the optional count still runs. Supply a stable, fully unique ordering to your data source. For a classic pager, use `currentPage`, `lastPage`, and `pageName` to build links; pages do not contain URL links.

```json
{ "data": [ { "id": 21 } ], "currentPage": 2, "perPage": 20, "total": 95, "lastPage": 5, "from": 21, "to": 40, "hasMore": true, "pageName": "page" }
```

`from` and `to` are one-based and null on an empty page. The examples abbreviate the data array.

For example, a data source can implement numbered pages without exposing `IQueryable`:

```csharp
var page = await Pagination.PaginateAsync(
    request,
    (skip, take, ct) => store.FetchPostsAsync(skip, take, ct),
    ct => store.CountPostsAsync(ct),
    ct: cancellationToken);
```

For a React pager, use Inertia links and preserve any other filters your app needs:

```tsx
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/react'

{page.lastPage != null && Array.from({ length: page.lastPage }, (_, i) => i + 1).map((n) => (
  <Link key={n} href={`?${page.pageName}=${n}`} aria-current={n === page.currentPage ? 'page' : undefined}>
    {n}
  </Link>
))}
```

## Cursors

A cursor is a marker for the position of an item, useful when readers move forward and backward rather than jump to page numbers. The cursor overload of `PaginateAsync` takes a key selector and a fetch delegate. The delegate receives a decoded cursor with `Direction` (`After` or `Before`) and `Value`, a take count, and a cancellation token. Return rows in the requested direction, including up to one extra; the helper trims and reverses `Before` results to display order. Choose a stable unique non-null key. `hasMore` indicates more rows in the requested direction.

```json
{ "data": [ { "id": 21 } ], "perPage": 20, "nextCursor": "eyJ...", "previousCursor": null, "hasMore": true, "cursorName": "cursor" }
```

Cursors are URL-safe base64 of a compact JSON array: direction (`"a"` or `"b"`) followed by the key values. Supported keys are `int`, `long`, `Guid`, `string`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `decimal`, `double`, and `bool`. Cursors are **not tamper-proof**; apps that need tamper protection should wrap them with `IDataProtector`.

A malformed or foreign nonempty cursor falls back to the first page. When `CursorRequest.Logger` is set, the paginator logs this at Debug without cursor values or exception details. Minimal API binding uses configured pagination options and supplies a logger in the `Inertia.Net.Pagination` category when a logger factory is available. In MVC or FastEndpoints, `CursorRequest.From(HttpContext)` does the same; optional arguments override the configured defaults and parameter names. For a query-only request or a request created outside HTTP, supply an app logger explicitly:

```csharp
var request = CursorRequest.From(query) with { Logger = logger };
```

`Logger` is ignored by JSON serialization and does not affect request equality.

## Defer or cache a page

A page can use the same prop modifiers as other values. For example, `Scroll(ct => Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, fetch, ct: ct)).Defer()` loads it after the first response; a lazy prop can also use `.Cache(...)`. See [Deferred props](/docs/deferred-props) and [Props](/docs/props) for loader and cache options.

## With EF Core

If your app uses EF Core, install the optional package alongside your database provider:

```sh
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.EntityFrameworkCore --version 1.7.0
```

The following uses an existing `AppDb` as `db`, with a `Posts` set. `request` is a `PageRequest`, `cursorRequest` is a `CursorRequest`, and `ct` is the request cancellation token:

```csharp
using Inertia.Net;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

// Numbered pages: order first, including a unique tie-breaker if needed.
var page = await db.Posts.OrderByDescending(p => p.Id)
    .ToPageAsync(request, ct: ct);

// Cursor pages: pass an unordered query. The helper applies the ordering.
var cursorPage = await db.Posts
    .ToCursorPageAsync(p => p.CreatedAt, p => p.Id, cursorRequest,
        descending: true, ct: ct);

return Render("Feed", new InertiaProps { ["posts"] = Scroll(cursorPage) });
```

Both results contain the selected group in `data`. A cursor is a marker: send it back unchanged to request the next or previous group. `ToPageAsync` requires an ordered query and counts rows by default; pass `countTotal: false` to skip the count and return null `total` and `lastPage`. `ToCursorPageAsync` rejects an already ordered query and orders by the supplied key and optional tie-breaker itself. Both guards throw `InvalidOperationException`. The cursor helper fetches in both directions without counting.

Choose a stable, fully unique ordering: use a unique key, or add a unique tie-breaker when the first key can repeat. Nullable keys are unsupported. The cursor codec supports the types listed above, but EF translation and ordering for each type depend on the database provider; for example, SQLite needs a suitable value conversion to order `DateTimeOffset`. The name from a bound request or `From(...)` is used for the corresponding page parameter; an explicit `pageName` or `cursorName` argument takes precedence.

The EF Core package is not marked Native AOT compatible. EF Core has its own compiled-model requirements; for Native AOT applications, use the core delegate paginators with an AOT-compatible data source instead.

## Native AOT

Register each closed page type in your app's `JsonSerializerContext` along with the item types:

```csharp
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<PostDto>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(CursorPage<PostDto>))]
```

See [Native AOT](/docs/native-aot).

## Caching and scroll props

A cached page still writes its scroll metadata. Use cache keys that include the page or cursor and all user or tenant dependencies. `Scroll(...)` can be deferred or cached; do not reuse its mutable prop instance across requests. Root `Append()` and `Prepend()` cannot be combined on the same prop. See [Props](/docs/props#cached-props) and [Infinite scroll](/docs/infinite-scroll).

---

# Live props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/live-props

> Props that refresh themselves when the server broadcasts an event.

A live prop refreshes itself when the server broadcasts an event. The page response says which props listen to which events; the client subscribes to those channels and, when an event arrives, reloads the affected props or applies the values the event carries. Components never subscribe or clean up.

Three pieces make it work:

1. **An event**, defined once as a `LiveEvent` and shared by both sides.
2. **A prop marked `.Live(event)`**, which puts its listeners in the page's `liveProps`.
3. **A publish** through `IInertiaLive`, delivered to subscribers by a transport.

<Callout type="info" title="Client version">
Live props need `@inertiajs/react`, `@inertiajs/vue3` or `@inertiajs/svelte` 3.11.0 or later. Older clients ignore `liveProps`.
</Callout>

## Define each event once

A `LiveEvent` is an event name on a `LiveChannel`. The same value declares the prop and publishes the event, so the two sides cannot drift apart.

```csharp
public static class OrderEvents
{
    public static LiveEvent Updated(int id) => new("OrderUpdated", LiveChannel.Private($"orders.{id}"));
    public static LiveEvent StatsChanged { get; } = new("StatsChanged", LiveChannel.Public("stats"));
}
```

Channels are `LiveChannel.Public`, `Private`, `Presence` or `EncryptedPrivate`. Names carry no prefix; a transport adds `private-` or `presence-` itself when its protocol needs one.

## Mark props live

```csharp
app.MapGet("/orders/{id:int}", (int id, AppDb db) => Render("Orders/Show", new InertiaProps
{
    ["order"]   = Prop(ct => db.Orders.SingleAsync(o => o.Id == id, ct))
                      .Live(OrderEvents.Updated(id))
                      .Throttle(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500)),
    ["metrics"] = Defer(ct => metrics.ForOrderAsync(id, ct)).Live(OrderEvents.Updated(id)),
    ["stats"]   = Optional(() => stats.Today()).Live(OrderEvents.StatsChanged),
}));
```

The page lists every listener, including those of props it left out:

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "order": { "id": 1, "status": "paid" } },
  "deferredProps": { "default": ["metrics"] },
  "liveProps": {
    "order": {
      "listeners": [
        { "channel": { "name": "orders.1", "type": "private" }, "events": ["OrderUpdated"] }
      ],
      "throttle": 500
    },
    "metrics": {
      "listeners": [
        { "channel": { "name": "orders.1", "type": "private" }, "events": ["OrderUpdated"] }
      ]
    },
    "stats": {
      "listeners": [
        { "channel": { "name": "stats", "type": "public" }, "events": ["StatsChanged"] }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

| Call | Effect |
|---|---|
| `.Live(event)` | Adds a listener. Repeatable: call it once per event. |
| `.Live(channel, "Created", "Deleted")` | Listens to several events on one channel. |
| `Live(() => ..., event)` | The factory form of `Prop(...).Live(event)`. |
| `.Throttle(window)` | The shortest time between two reloads of the prop. The client's default is one second. |

### What combines with live

| Prop | Live? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Prop`, `Always`, shared props | Yes | |
| `Defer`, `Optional` | Yes | Listeners are reported even while the value is left out. |
| `Once` | Yes | A once prop the client already holds stays subscribed. |
| `Rescue`, `Parallel` | Yes | A rescued prop stays subscribed; the next event fetches it again. |
| `Cache` | Yes | Publishing does not evict the cache. Remove the entry with `IInertiaCache` first. |
| `Merge`, `DeepMerge`, `Scroll` | No | A live prop is replaced whole, so these throw `InvalidOperationException`. |

A live prop inside an array reloads its whole array, as every [partial reload](/docs/partial-reloads) of an array descendant does. Prefer keyed objects for lists that change often.

## Shared live props

A shared live prop keeps something current on every page, such as a notification bell:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.Share("notifications", ctx =>
{
    var userId = ctx.User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier);
    return userId is null ? null : Prop(ct => notifications.SummaryAsync(userId, ct))
        .Live(new LiveEvent("NotificationCreated", LiveChannel.Private($"users.{userId}")));
}));
```

## Publish events

`AddInertiaLive()` registers `IInertiaLive`. A transport registers the `IInertiaLiveBroadcaster` that delivers what it publishes.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaLive();   // then a transport: .AddSignalR() or your own IInertiaLiveBroadcaster
```

<Tabs>
<Tab label="Reload">

```csharp
// Everyone else on the channel reloads `order`; the caller already has the response.
app.MapPost("/orders/{id:int}/ship", async (int id, HttpContext context, IInertiaLive live) =>
{
    await orders.ShipAsync(id);
    await live.PublishAsync(OrderEvents.Updated(id), exceptSocketId: context.InertiaRequest().SocketId);
    return Back();
});
```

</Tab>
<Tab label="With values">

```csharp
// Clients apply the value without a request; live props left out are reloaded.
await live.PublishAsync(OrderEvents.Updated(order.Id), new { order = OrderDto.From(order) });
```

</Tab>
<Tab label="Explicit metadata">

```csharp
// Written with that context's own options, as JsonSerializer would.
await live.PublishAsync(OrderEvents.Updated(order.Id), new OrderProps(dto), AppJsonContext.Default.OrderProps);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

- **Without values**, every client reloads the live props that listen to the event, each with its own request and its own data.
- **With values**, keyed by prop path (`"auth.user"` stays a flat key), those props are updated in place. Values use the page serializer options, so they match what a reload returns; under Native AOT the type needs to be in your registered JSON context, like any prop type.
- **`exceptSocketId`** leaves one connection out, usually the client that made the change. The client sends its id as `X-Socket-Id` and `HttpContext.InertiaRequest().SocketId` reads it. The header is client-supplied, so it is only ever used to exclude.

<Callout type="danger" title="Every subscriber sees the same values">
A broadcast reaches every client on the channel. Only publish values that everyone allowed on the channel may see. When a value depends on the user, publish without values and let each client reload its own.
</Callout>

What a broadcaster delivers:

```json
{
  "__inertia": {
    "event": "OrderUpdated",
    "props": { "order": { "id": 1, "status": "shipped" } }
  }
}
```

## On the client

Read a live prop like any other prop. `useProp` exposes its loading state, and the cancelable `live` router event can hold an update back, for example to show a "new posts" button instead:

```tsx
import { router, useProp } from '@inertiajs/react'

const order = useProp<Order>('order')   // { value, loading, loaded }

router.on('live', (event) => {
  if (event.detail.props.includes('posts')) {
    showNewPostsButton()
    return false
  }
})
```

## SignalR

`Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR` runs the transport inside your app: a SignalR hub the browser subscribes to, channel authorization, and the broadcaster that `IInertiaLive` publishes through.

```sh
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR
npm install @microsoft/signalr # or: bun add, pnpm add, yarn add @microsoft/signalr
```

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaLive().AddSignalR(o =>
    o.Authorize((context, channel, ct) =>
        ValueTask.FromResult(channel.Name == $"users.{context.UserIdentifier}")));

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.UseInertia();
app.MapInertiaLiveHub();   // /inertia-live
```

Apps created with `dotnet new inertia` ship the client transport as `ClientApp/lib/inertia-signalr.ts`. In other apps, copy [the file](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/src/Inertia.Net.Templates/content/common/ClientApp/lib/inertia-signalr.ts) in, then turn it on:

```ts
import { signalr } from './lib/inertia-signalr'

createInertiaApp({ live: signalr() })
```

`@microsoft/signalr` loads on the first subscription, so pages without live props never download it. When a dropped connection comes back, the transport joins its channels again and Inertia reloads every live prop once, catching up on missed events.

### Who may join a channel

| Channel | Who joins |
|---|---|
| `Public` | Anyone who reaches the hub. Set `o.AuthorizePublicChannels = true` to ask the authorizer too. |
| `Private`, `Presence`, `EncryptedPrivate` | Only connections the authorizer allows. With no authorizer, nobody. |

For rules that need services, implement `ILiveChannelAuthorizer` and register it with `o.Authorize<OrderChannelAuthorizer>()`. It is created for each subscription, with constructor injection. SignalR has no presence member lists or end-to-end encryption, so presence and encrypted-private channels are authorized like private ones.

The hub answers requests from other origins with 403 (add trusted ones to `o.AllowedOrigins`). That check stands in for antiforgery tokens on the hub. Connections close when their authentication expires.

<Callout type="warning" title="More than one server">
SignalR groups live on one server. Behind several instances, add a Redis backplane (`AddSignalR().AddStackExchangeRedis(...)`) or Azure SignalR Service; without one, a publish reaches only the clients connected to the instance that sent it.
</Callout>

The [package README](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/src/Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR/README.md) lists the client options, how channels map to SignalR groups, and the security notes.

## Custom transports

The page metadata and the payload do not depend on SignalR, so any transport works:

- **Pusher-protocol servers** (Reverb, Soketi, Ably, Pusher) work with the client's built-in `pusher()` or `echo()` transport. On the server, implement `IInertiaLiveBroadcaster` with your server's publish API.
- **Anything else** (Action Cable, server-sent events, Azure Web PubSub): implement `IInertiaLiveBroadcaster` on the server and a `LiveTransport` on the client.

A broadcaster has one method. It receives the channel, the finished payload and the connection to skip:

```csharp
public sealed class MyBroadcaster : IInertiaLiveBroadcaster
{
    public ValueTask PublishAsync(LiveMessage message, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        // message.Channel.Key:      "private:orders.1"
        // message.Payload:          {"__inertia":{"event":"OrderUpdated",...}}, a JsonElement
        // message.ExceptSocketId:   the connection to leave out, or null
        throw new NotImplementedException("Send message.Payload to the channel's subscribers.");
    }
}
```

## Testing

`InertiaPage.LiveProps` holds the metadata, and `HasLive` asserts it, with the channel written as `"{type}:{name}"`:

```csharp
await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page
    .HasLive("order")
    .HasLive("order", "private:orders.1", "OrderUpdated"));
```

## Limits, proxies and authorization changes

SignalR defaults to 64 subscriptions per connection and a 200-character channel name. Configure `MaxSubscriptionsPerConnection` and `MaxChannelNameLength` through the SignalR options; both must be positive. Behind a TLS-terminating proxy configure trusted forwarded headers once and run `UseForwardedHeaders()` before the hub so origin and scheme checks see the external address.

Authorization is checked when a client subscribes, not continuously. If access changes, disconnect the client or use a transport/application strategy that enforces revocation. A `removed` event can tell the UI to update, but it is not a security revocation mechanism.

---

# Precognition

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/precognition

> Validate a form before submission without running its handler.

The [Minimal API React sample](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/tree/main/samples/MinimalApi.React) includes a login validation demo. It accepts dummy values and does not create an authentication session. Precognition sends the same POST as the form with `Precognition: true`. The server validates it and returns without running the handler:

```http
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Precognition: true
Precognition-Validate-Only: email
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"invalid","password":"password123"}

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Precognition: true
Vary: Precognition
Content-Type: application/json

{"message":"The Email field is not a valid e-mail address.","errors":{"email":["The Email field is not a valid e-mail address."]}}
```

The `message` is the first returned error. A valid request returns `204` and `Precognition-Success: true`. For Minimal APIs register `AddValidation()` and use:

```csharp
app.MapPost("/login", (LoginForm input) => Back().WithFlash("success", "Demo form submitted"))
   .WithInertiaPrecognition();
```

The sample's input model is:

```csharp
public sealed class LoginForm
{
    [Required, EmailAddress]
    public string? Email { get; set; }

    [Required, MinLength(8)]
    public string? Password { get; set; }
}
```

Import `System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations`. This replaces `.WithInertiaValidation()`; do not use both. It also handles normal validation redirects. Filters added after it do not run on precognitive requests. FastEndpoints enables this through `c.ConfigureInertia()`; MVC does not support Precognition.

## Client setup

Inertia 3 includes Precognition in its form integration. Each example validates on blur and displays the error:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { useEffect } from 'react'

export default function LoginForm() {
  const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '' }).withPrecognition('post', '/login')
  useEffect(() => { form.setValidationTimeout(3000) }, [])
  return (
    <form onSubmit={e => { e.preventDefault(); form.post('/login') }}>
      <label>Email <input value={form.data.email} onChange={e => form.setData('email', e.target.value)}
        onBlur={() => form.validate('email')} /></label>
      <label>Password <input type="password" value={form.data.password} onChange={e => form.setData('password', e.target.value)}
        onBlur={() => form.validate('password')} /></label>
      {form.errors.password && <p>{form.errors.password}</p>}
      {form.validating && <span>Validating…</span>}
      {form.errors.email && <p>{form.errors.email}</p>}
      <button type="submit">Submit demo</button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup>
import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '' }).withPrecognition('post', '/login')
form.setValidationTimeout(3000)
</script>
<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="form.post('/login')">
    <label>Email <input v-model="form.email" @blur="form.validate('email')" /></label>
    <label>Password <input v-model="form.password" type="password" @blur="form.validate('password')" /></label>
    <p v-if="form.errors.password">{{ form.errors.password }}</p>
    <button type="submit">Submit demo</button>
  </form>
  <span v-if="form.validating">Validating…</span>
  <p v-if="form.errors.email">{{ form.errors.email }}</p>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script>
  import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/svelte'
  const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '' }).withPrecognition('post', '/login')
  form.setValidationTimeout(3000)
</script>
<form onsubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); form.post('/login') }}>
  <label>Email <input bind:value={form.email} onblur={() => form.validate('email')} /></label>
  <label>Password <input type="password" bind:value={form.password} onblur={() => form.validate('password')} /></label>
  {#if form.errors.password}<p>{form.errors.password}</p>{/if}
  <button type="submit">Submit demo</button>
</form>
{#if form.validating}<span>Validating…</span>{/if}
{#if form.errors.email}<p>{form.errors.email}</p>{/if}
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

`Precognition-Validate-Only` selects returned errors by field, including nested paths. Validation still runs the validator: keep database rules cheap. Validate on blur for login and payment forms to avoid an error while the user is still typing. `setValidationTimeout(3000)` raises the debounce interval for expensive rules; it is not the HTTP deadline.

## Antiforgery and authorization

`UseInertiaAntiforgery()` validates precognitive POSTs like other unsafe requests; the Inertia client sends the token automatically. Authorization middleware runs before endpoint filters, so protected forms validate only for authorized users.

## Rate limiting

Precognitive POSTs pass through rate limiting before the endpoint filter, so using a single strict login bucket can lock users out while typing. Use separate bounded partitions for validation and real submissions, and check endpoint `InertiaPrecognitionMetadata` as well as `InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(request)`: the header alone does not guarantee the handler is skipped. Do not use `GetNoLimiter` for validation; validators consume CPU and may query a database. With the metadata present the handler is skipped, so the validation bucket does not allow credential attempts.

On a rejected precognitive request set `Precognition: true` on the 429 response. This lets the client recognize the response; the validation request still rejects, so provide a retry or error message. Run `UseRouting`, `UseRateLimiter`, `UseInertia` and `UseInertiaAntiforgery` in that order. See the example below for a complete policy.

The following `AddServices` method is copied from the Minimal API sample's `LoginDemo` class. The sample's `_generation` field exists only to reset E2E test buckets; real apps can partition on a stable client identity appropriate to their deployment. Import `System.Globalization`, `System.Threading.RateLimiting` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting`, and declare `private static int _generation;` and `private static int _submissions;` in that class. The [complete sample class](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/samples/MinimalApi.React/LoginDemo.cs) includes `LoginForm`, `LoginPage`, and the reset helper:

```csharp
    public static void AddServices(IServiceCollection services)
    {
        services.AddRateLimiter(options =>
        {
            options.RejectionStatusCode = StatusCodes.Status429TooManyRequests;
            options.AddPolicy("login", http =>
            {
                var validation = http.GetEndpoint()?.Metadata.GetMetadata<InertiaPrecognitionMetadata>() is not null
                    && InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(http.Request);
                var client = http.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "unknown";
                // The generation lets the sample's E2E reset endpoint give each test fresh buckets.
                var generation = Volatile.Read(ref _generation);
                if (validation)
                {
                    return RateLimitPartition.GetSlidingWindowLimiter($"validation:{client}:{generation}", _ => new SlidingWindowRateLimiterOptions
                    {
                        PermitLimit = 30,
                        Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1),
                        SegmentsPerWindow = 6,
                        QueueLimit = 0,
                    });
                }

                return RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter($"submit:{client}:{generation}", _ => new FixedWindowRateLimiterOptions
                {
                    PermitLimit = 5,
                    Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1),
                    QueueLimit = 0,
                });
            });
            options.OnRejected = (context, _) =>
            {
                var http = context.HttpContext;
                if (http.GetEndpoint()?.Metadata.GetMetadata<InertiaPrecognitionMetadata>() is not null
                    && InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(http.Request))
                {
                    http.Response.Headers[InertiaPrecognition.Header] = "true";
                    http.Response.Headers.Append("Vary", InertiaPrecognition.Header);
                }

                if (context.Lease.TryGetMetadata(MetadataName.RetryAfter, out var retryAfter))
                    http.Response.Headers.RetryAfter = Math.Ceiling(retryAfter.TotalSeconds).ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
            };
        });
    }
```

Register it before building the app. The sample also opts 429 into error-page handling for real Inertia submissions; 429 is not a default error-page status:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaErrorPages(o => o.StatusCodes.Add(429));
```

Map an error page with a retry message. Precognitive requests accepting JSON retain their 429 response and `Precognition: true` header. Attach the policy to the endpoint:

```csharp
LoginDemo.AddServices(builder.Services);
// After builder.Build():
app.UseInertiaErrorPages(); // wraps rate-limit and page responses
app.UseRouting();
app.UseRateLimiter();
app.UseInertia();
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(); // after UseAuthentication() in an app with sign-in
LoginDemo.MapRoutes(app);
```

The sample routes use this method:

```csharp
    public static void MapRoutes(WebApplication app)
    {
        app.MapGet("/login", () => Render("Login", new LoginPage(Volatile.Read(ref _submissions))));
        app.MapPost("/login", (LoginForm input) =>
        {
            Interlocked.Increment(ref _submissions);
            return Back().WithFlash("success", "Demo form submitted");
        }).WithInertiaPrecognition().RequireRateLimiting("login");
    }
```

The sample partitions by remote IP for demonstration; configure trusted forwarded headers when behind a proxy and choose a partition key suited to your authentication and abuse model.

## Testing

With an `Inertia.Net.Testing` client that retains cookies, load the form page and attach its XSRF token. For an endpoint that validates `email`:

```csharp
client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Accept.ParseAdd("text/html");
using var page = await client.GetAsync("/login");
async Task<HttpResponseMessage> ValidateAsync(string email)
{
    using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/login")
    {
        Content = JsonContent.Create(new { email, password = "password123" }),
    };
    request.WithXsrfToken(page);
    request.Headers.Add(InertiaPrecognition.Header, "true");
    request.Headers.Add(InertiaPrecognition.ValidateOnlyHeader, "email");
    return await client.SendAsync(request);
}
using var valid = await ValidateAsync("ann@example.com");
Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.NoContent, valid.StatusCode);
Assert.Equal("true", valid.Headers.GetValues(InertiaPrecognition.SuccessHeader).Single());
using var invalid = await ValidateAsync("invalid");
Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableEntity, invalid.StatusCode);
using var body = JsonDocument.Parse(await invalid.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
Assert.True(body.RootElement.GetProperty("errors").TryGetProperty("email", out _));
```

Import `System.Net`, `System.Net.Http.Json`, `System.Text.Json`, `Inertia.Net` and `Inertia.Net.Testing`. [Testing](/docs/testing#testing-a-form-with-antiforgery) shows the client and token setup.

## Protocol reference

| Header | Direction | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Precognition: true` | Request and response | Identifies a validation request and response |
| `Precognition-Validate-Only` | Request | Comma-separated client field paths whose errors are returned |
| `Precognition-Success: true` | Response | Validation succeeded (204) |
| `Vary: Precognition` | Response | Varies the response by request type |

A validation failure returns `422`; a limiter may return `429`. `InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(HttpRequest)` checks the header; `InertiaPrecognitionMetadata` identifies endpoints whose handler is skipped for these requests.

---

# Server-side rendering

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/server-side-rendering

> Render the first visit on Bun or Node, supervise the process from .NET, and fall back safely.

SSR renders the first visit on a JavaScript server using your client bundle, so crawlers and slow devices get HTML. Inertia XHR requests are never rendered on the server.

## 1. Build the SSR bundle

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="@inertiajs/vite">

```tsx
// ClientApp/ssr.tsx
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'

createInertiaApp()
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import inertia from '@inertiajs/vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    inertia({
      ssr: { entry: 'ClientApp/ssr.tsx', host: '127.0.0.1', port: 13714 },
    }),
  ],
})
```

Build both bundles:

```json
{ "scripts": { "build": "vite build && vite build --ssr" } }
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Manual entry">

```tsx
// resources/js/ssr.tsx
import { createInertiaApp, type ResolvedComponent } from '@inertiajs/react'
import createServer from '@inertiajs/react/server'
import ReactDOMServer from 'react-dom/server'

createServer((page) =>
  createInertiaApp({
    page,
    render: ReactDOMServer.renderToString,
    resolve: (name) => {
      const pages = import.meta.glob<{ default: ResolvedComponent }>('./Pages/**/*.tsx', { eager: true })
      return pages[`./Pages/${name}.tsx`]
    },
    setup: ({ App, props }) => <App {...props} />,
  }),
  { host: '127.0.0.1', port: Number(process.env.INERTIA_SSR_PORT ?? 13714) },
)
```

The client entry hydrates when the server rendered:

```tsx
import { createRoot, hydrateRoot } from 'react-dom/client'

setup({ el, App, props }) {
  if (!el) throw new Error('Inertia root element not found')
  if (el.dataset.serverRendered === 'true') hydrateRoot(el, <App {...props} />)
  else createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />)
}
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Run the bundle with Bun or Node, or let the app start it:

```sh
bun ssr/ssr.js        # listens on http://127.0.0.1:13714
# or
node ssr/ssr.js
```

Build and run from a directory with `node_modules` installed. The SSR build leaves `node_modules` imports external.

## 2. Enable it

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Ssr.Mode = SsrMode.Preferred;                  // Disabled (default), Preferred or Required
    o.Ssr.Urls.Add("http://127.0.0.1:13714");       // default when empty; add more servers to spread renders
    o.Ssr.ConnectTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);  // connection establishment
    o.Ssr.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);         // total deadline per render
    o.Ssr.MaxPageBytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024;            // larger pages render on the client without a call
    o.Ssr.MaxResponseBytes = 16L * 1024 * 1024;      // success and error responses
    o.Ssr.BundlePath = "ssr/ssr.js";                 // skip SSR while this file does not exist
    o.Ssr.ExcludePaths.Add("/admin/*");              // exact, or a trailing * for a prefix
});
```

A response can choose its own mode:

```csharp
return Render("Checkout").WithoutSsr();
return Render("Landing").WithSsr(SsrMode.Required);
return Render("Admin/Home").WithSsr(SsrMode.Preferred);
```

The global mode decides first: `Disabled` is a kill switch no response can override. Otherwise the response's mode wins, then `ExcludePaths`, then the global mode.

SSR runs only for first visits (the HTML response). The page JSON is posted to `{url}/render`, and `{ "head": [...], "body": "..." }` is written into the root view. `@inertiaHead` outputs the head tags; `@inertia` outputs the body.

## 3. Let the app run Bun or Node

```csharp
o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess();          // also sets Mode = Preferred when it is Disabled
o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n =>
{
    n.BundlePath = "ssr/ssr.js";
    n.Executable = "node";
    n.Arguments.Add("--enable-source-maps");
    n.WorkingDirectory = null;                   // default: content root
    n.StartupTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
    n.RestartOnExit = true;
    n.Instances = 1;                             // instance i listens on BasePort + i
    n.BasePort = 13714;
    n.LivenessInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);
    n.LivenessFailureThreshold = 3;
    n.AllowNetworkExposure = false;
});
```

A hosted service runs `{Executable} {bundle}` (`node` by default; Bun works too) once per instance, logs stdout as Information and stderr as Warning under `Inertia.Net.Ssr`, and waits for every instance's `GET /health`. Occupied ports are refused before anything is spawned. `Ssr.Urls` is not used in managed mode.

<Callout type="tip" title="Bun works too">
The executable is configurable. This documentation site builds a self-contained SSR bundle and runs it with Bun: `o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n => n.Executable = "bun")`. The default is `node`; the bundle accepts either runtime.
</Callout>

- An instance that exits is restarted after 1 second, doubling to 30 seconds.
- An instance that stops answering its liveness check is killed and restarted the same way.
- Shutdown stops the owned process trees without requesting `/shutdown`.
- Nothing is spawned while the Vite dev server runs.
- For external or remote servers, set `Mode` and `Urls` without `UseNodeProcess()`.

<Callout type="danger" title="Keep the SSR server on loopback">
The SSR server has no authentication. Anyone who can reach it can `POST /render` (CPU) or `POST /shutdown`, and its `head` and `body` are written into your pages verbatim. Listen on `127.0.0.1`. Before an instance takes renders, Inertia.Net tries the machine's non-loopback addresses on its port. If the instance answers there, it is stopped and an error is logged. `AllowNetworkExposure = true` keeps it running with a warning.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warning" title="Orphans">
A graceful shutdown stops the SSR process. If the .NET process is killed outright, the OS does not take the runtime with it. Use a process manager or container for hard-crash cleanup.
</Callout>

## 4. Development

With the Vite hot file present (Development only), or `o.Vite.DevServerUrl` set, Inertia.Net posts to `{viteDevUrl}/__inertia_ssr`. The endpoint is served by `@inertiajs/vite`, so you need no built bundle and no separate SSR server.

```ts
import inertia from '@inertiajs/vite'

inertia({ ssr: { entry: 'resources/js/ssr.tsx', host: '127.0.0.1', port: 13714 } })
```

`BundlePath` is ignored while the dev server runs.

## 5. Failures and fallbacks

In `Preferred` mode every failure logs a warning and the page renders on the client. In `Required` mode it throws `InertiaSsrException` before the first byte is written, so the app's exception handler can still answer.

| Type | Cause | Opens the circuit |
|---|---|---|
| `connection` | Connection refused or reset. A refused connection is retried on another server. | yes |
| `timeout` | `Ssr.Timeout` elapsed | yes |
| `http` | Non-2xx answer without a structured error | yes |
| `response` | Empty or malformed answer | yes |
| `render` | The component threw (structured error from the renderer) | no |
| `response-too-large` | Answer over `MaxResponseBytes` | no |
| `overloaded` | No render slot within `Concurrency.QueueTimeout`, or the queue is full | no |
| `circuit-open`, `not-ready`, `page-too-large`, `bundle-missing` | Skipped without a call | no |

**Circuit breaker.** After `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` (default 5) consecutive failures that open the circuit, a server is skipped for `BreakDuration` (default 10 s). Then one render probes it: success closes the circuit, failure starts another break. A page that fails because of its own code never pauses the server.

**Render slots.** Each server takes at most `Concurrency.MaxActive` renders at once (default 8, `0` for no limit) from this app instance, with up to `MaxQueued` (default 32) waiting at most `QueueTimeout` (default 250 ms). Renders that find no slot fall back immediately.

## 6. Several servers

```csharp
o.Ssr.Urls.Add("http://ssr-1:13714");
o.Ssr.Urls.Add("http://ssr-2:13714");
```

Each render goes to the server with the fewest renders in flight among those whose circuit is closed (ties rotate). Every server has its own slots, queue and circuit. Only a refused connection is retried on another server within the same deadline.

Page props travel to the renderer, and its HTML goes into your pages unescaped, so it must be trusted. A plain `http://` URL that is not loopback logs a warning at startup. Use HTTPS or a private network.

## 7. Health check

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddInertiaSsr();
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

The check reports what the renders have already shown, without calling the SSR servers: healthy while SSR is disabled, goes through the Vite dev server, or every server can take renders; degraded while some circuits are open or some managed instances are not ready; the registration's failure status (default unhealthy) when none can. Its data lists each server's state.

## 8. Observability

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
    .WithMetrics(m => m.AddMeter(InertiaDiagnostics.MeterName))
    .WithTracing(t => t.AddSource(InertiaDiagnostics.ActivitySourceName));
```

| Instrument | Type | Tags |
|---|---|---|
| `inertia.page.duration` (s) | histogram | `inertia.response`, `inertia.partial` |
| `inertia.page.size` (By) | histogram | `inertia.response` |
| `inertia.ssr.duration` (s) | histogram | `inertia.ssr.outcome` |
| `inertia.ssr.queue.duration` (s) | histogram | |
| `inertia.ssr.active` | up-down counter | |
| `inertia.ssr.outcomes` | counter | `inertia.ssr.outcome`, `inertia.ssr.reason` |
| `inertia.ssr.response.size` (By) | histogram | |
| `inertia.ssr.circuit.state` | gauge | `inertia.ssr.endpoint` |
| `inertia.ssr.circuit.transitions` | counter | `inertia.ssr.endpoint`, `to` |
| `inertia.ssr.process.restarts` | counter | `cause` |
| `inertia.props.rescued` | counter | |

Tag values are bounded: no URLs, component names or user data. The `inertia.render` activity carries `inertia.component`; the `inertia.ssr` activity carries `inertia.ssr.endpoint`, `inertia.ssr.outcome` and `inertia.ssr.reason`. Nothing is recorded unless a listener is attached.

## 9. Response cache

A render depends only on the page JSON, so a page that many visitors see byte for byte the same can reuse its HTML:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Ssr.Cache.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
    o.Ssr.Cache.StaleFor = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30);
    o.Ssr.Cache.MaxBytes = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
});

return Render("Pricing", props).WithSsrCache(TimeSpan.FromHours(1));
return Render("Pricing", props).WithSsrCache(TimeSpan.FromHours(1), staleFor: TimeSpan.FromDays(1));
```

The key is the SHA-256 of the page JSON (component, props, url, version and the rest), so a new deploy or different props never reuse a stale render. Pages with per-user props make one entry per user; cache the pages that are shared. A hit is counted as `inertia.ssr.outcomes{inertia.ssr.outcome=rendered, inertia.ssr.reason=cache}` and bypasses the render slots and circuit breakers. Nothing is cached while the Vite dev server renders.

Concurrent misses for the same page share one fill per app instance. Waiting counts against `Ssr.Timeout`; cancelling a waiting request does not cancel the request filling the entry.

With `StaleFor`, a render past its `Duration` is still served and refreshed by the bounded background worker after response completion, like stale props. The connection can accept its next request while the renderer runs. Refreshes cancel when the host stops. If the 64-entry queue is full, the refresh is dropped and logged; monitor `inertia.cache.refresh.dropped` with `inertia.cache.kind=ssr`. `IInertiaCache.ClearSsrAsync()` removes every render.

`Ssr.ConnectTimeout` bounds connection establishment independently of `Ssr.Timeout`; both accept a positive duration or `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`. In Required mode, `InertiaSsrException.Message` contains a generic failure category suitable for an error page. Renderer diagnostics remain in application logs and diagnostic exception properties; do not expose those properties to clients.

## Connection timeout and cached renders

`Ssr.ConnectTimeout` defaults to five seconds and limits connection establishment; `Ssr.Timeout` bounds the entire render. In `Required` mode, exceptions use a generic public message; diagnostic properties can contain private renderer details, so do not display them to users.

A stale SSR cache hit returns immediately and schedules refresh on a bounded background worker. Its queue holds 64 pending refreshes; a dropped refresh logs a warning and increments `inertia.cache.refresh.dropped` with `inertia.cache.kind=ssr`. Cached prop loaders used with stale refresh must use singleton dependencies or create their own scope; never capture request-scoped services or `HttpContext`. Global `Ssr.Cache.Duration` is suitable for anonymous pages. Prefer per-page `WithSsrCache` and keys that account for all user and tenant data.

---

# Vite

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/vite-integration

> Manifest tags, the dev-server hot file, asset base URLs, prefetching and CSP nonces.

`ViteAssets` (a singleton, also usable directly as `vite.RenderTags(httpContext, "resources/js/app.tsx")`) renders the tags for the `@vite(...)` token and the `<vite />` tag helper.

## Production

In production Inertia.Net reads `wwwroot/build/.vite/manifest.json` (falling back to `wwwroot/build/manifest.json` for older Vite). It parses the manifest once and pre-renders the tags to UTF-8. For each entry it emits, in order:

1. `<link rel="stylesheet">` for the entry's CSS and the CSS of its static imports, recursively and deduplicated;
2. `<script type="module" src="...">` for the entry file;
3. `<link rel="modulepreload">` for each static import.

URLs are `{PathBase}/{BuildDirectory}/{file}` so apps under a path base work, or `{AssetBaseUrl}/{file}`. An entry missing from the manifest throws with the list of available entries. A missing manifest throws with the paths it looked in.

## Development

While the dev server runs, the tags are `@vite/client` and the entry from the dev server origin, plus the React Refresh preamble for `@viteReactRefresh`. The dev server counts as running when:

- `o.Vite.DevServerUrl` is set (always, in any environment), or
- the environment is Development and the hot file (`wwwroot/hot` by default) exists and contains the origin.

The hot file is written by your Vite config. The `@inertiajs/vite` plugin does not write one, so the samples include a small plugin that does.

<Callout type="warning" title="base must differ between dev and build">
Built assets are served from `/build/`, so the Vite `base` is `/build/` for a build. The dev server must serve from the root because Inertia.Net emits `{origin}/@vite/client` and `{origin}/{entry}`. Use `base: command === 'build' ? '/build/' : '/'`.
</Callout>

## Options

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Vite.PublicDirectory = "wwwroot";                        // default
    o.Vite.BuildDirectory = "build";                           // default
    o.Vite.ManifestPath = null;                                // default wwwroot/build/.vite/manifest.json
    o.Vite.HotFilePath = null;                                 // default wwwroot/hot
    o.Vite.DevServerUrl = builder.Environment.IsDevelopment() ? "http://localhost:5173" : null;
    o.Vite.AssetBaseUrl = "https://cdn.example.com/build";     // serve built assets from a CDN
});
```

Only plain http(s) origins without quotes or markup are accepted from the hot file or `DevServerUrl`, because the origin is echoed into a script.

With `AssetBaseUrl` set, Vite's own `base` must match so lazily imported chunks resolve against the CDN too:

```ts
base: 'https://cdn.example.com/build/'
```

## Prefetching

Page components resolved with lazy `import.meta.glob` are separate chunks that the browser downloads only when a page needs them. `o.Vite.Prefetch` downloads them after the page loads, at low priority, so the next navigation does not wait:

```csharp
o.Vite.Prefetch = VitePrefetch.Waterfall;   // PrefetchConcurrency (default 3) at a time
o.Vite.Prefetch = VitePrefetch.Aggressive;  // all at once
```

The tags get one small inline script with the list of chunks the entries can import later (dynamic imports, then their static imports and CSS), minus those already loaded. It is rendered once per entry set.

## Content Security Policy

With a nonce-based CSP, set `o.CspNonce` to the request's nonce. Every script and stylesheet tag Inertia.Net writes then carries it: the page `<script data-page>`, the Vite tags, the React refresh preamble and the prefetch script (whose links get it too).

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.CspNonce = ctx => ctx.Items["csp-nonce"] as string);

app.Use((ctx, next) =>
{
    var nonce = Convert.ToBase64String(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16));
    ctx.Items["csp-nonce"] = nonce;
    ctx.Response.Headers.ContentSecurityPolicy =
        $"script-src 'nonce-{nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'";
    return next(ctx);
});
```

The nonce must be base64 or base64url; anything else throws. Cached tags are split where the nonce goes, so a nonce costs one copy of the tag bytes per request and no re-rendering.

<Callout type="tip" title="Static assets">
Use `app.UseStaticFiles()` with a long `Cache-Control` for `/build/assets`, or `app.MapStaticAssets()` when the client is built before `dotnet publish`. See [Deploying](/docs/deploying).
</Callout>

---

# Asset versioning

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/asset-versioning

> Tell the client when its JavaScript and CSS are stale, and reload once when they are.

The asset version tells the client when its assets are stale. The server resolves it in this order:

1. `InertiaOptions.VersionResolver(HttpContext)`, when it returns non-null;
2. else `InertiaOptions.Version`;
3. else a hash of the Vite manifest (the first 16 bytes of its SHA-256, in hex), computed once and recomputed in Development when the file changes;
4. else `""`.

```csharp
o.Version = typeof(Program).Assembly.GetName().Version!.ToString();       // or a build id
o.VersionResolver = ctx => ctx.Request.Headers["X-Tenant"].ToString();   // per request
```

## How the client checks it

When an Inertia **GET** carries a different `X-Inertia-Version`, the server answers `409` with `X-Inertia-Location` (the absolute request URL) and `X-Inertia-Version`, and the client performs a full page reload.

The check runs **before your handler**, so no work is wasted rendering a page that will be thrown away. Other methods never get this `409`.

```text
GET /users
X-Inertia: true
X-Inertia-Version: old

409 Conflict
X-Inertia-Location: https://example.com/users
X-Inertia-Version: new
```

## Choosing a version

- **Vite manifest hash (default).** Nothing to configure. A new build changes the manifest and the version.
- **Assembly version or build id.** Good when the client build is not tied to the manifest, or when several apps share assets.
- **Per-request version.** Useful for multi-tenant apps with different frontend builds per tenant.

<Callout type="danger" title="Never generate a new version on every request">
A `VersionResolver` that returns a random value on every call makes the client reload forever. Different instances behind a load balancer must serve the same build, or the client will bounce between versions.
</Callout>

## Path base

The version check and `X-Inertia-Location` use the request URL. Behind a path base or reverse proxy, configure forwarded headers so the scheme and host match the browser's URL. See [Deploying](/docs/deploying).

---

# CSRF protection

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/csrf-and-antiforgery

> Protect forms with the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.

The Inertia client reads the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and sends its value as the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on every request. `UseInertiaAntiforgery()` issues that cookie and validates it, so one call protects every form.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddAntiforgery(o => o.HeaderName = InertiaHeaders.XsrfToken);   // "X-XSRF-TOKEN"

app.UseAuthentication();                 // if the app signs users in: the token is bound to the signed-in user
app.UseInertia();
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery();
```

## What it does

- **Issue.** Page loads (GET/HEAD requests that are Inertia requests or accept `text/html`) get the request token in a script-readable, essential cookie (`HttpOnly` off, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, `Secure` per `SecurePolicy`). Essential means a cookie-consent policy does not withhold it.
- **Validate.** Every unsafe request (anything but GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE), with a JSON or a form body, Inertia or not, is checked with `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync`. A plain cross-site HTML form post is rejected as well as a forged XHR. It also sets the antiforgery feature, so form-binding endpoints work without `app.UseAntiforgery()`.
- **Reject.** A missing or wrong token gets **`419`** (page expired, as in Laravel); the handler does not run.
- **Opt out** per endpoint with `.DisableAntiforgery()` (webhooks, test hooks), or for whole areas with `ShouldValidate`.

## Options

```csharp
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(o =>
{
    o.CookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN";                                  // default
    o.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always;                   // default SameAsRequest
    o.ShouldValidate = ctx => !ctx.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/api");
    o.OnRejected = (ctx, error) => Back().WithFlash("error", "The page expired, please try again.");
});
```

`OnRejected` runs after `UseInertia()`; returning `Back()` gives the tab a fresh token and a message instead of the client's error dialog.

## Lazy refresh

By default every page load issues a fresh token, and antiforgery marks that response `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store` (which also keeps the page out of the browser's back/forward cache).

`o.CookieRefresh = XsrfCookieRefresh.Lazy` keeps a token that still validates. Such responses get no `Set-Cookie` and stay cacheable, and a token issued before a sign-in or sign-out is replaced on the next page load.

Validating costs about what issuing does, so the gain is in the responses, not in CPU. Set your own `Cache-Control` on pages with private data.

<Callout type="info" title="Session changes">
A session that expires or a sign-in that changes the user invalidates the token in an open tab; the next page load issues a new one. Returning `Back()` from `OnRejected` gives that tab a fresh token and a message.
</Callout>

## MVC and FastEndpoints

`UseInertiaAntiforgery()` covers controllers too. `[AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken]` as a global filter still works, but is not needed. FastEndpoints is covered by the middleware; FastEndpoints' own `EnableAntiforgery()` is not needed for Inertia forms.

## Issue only

`UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN")` (the 1.0 API) only writes the cookie. You then validate with `app.UseAntiforgery()` (form bodies only) and your own check for JSON bodies (`await antiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context)`). Prefer `UseInertiaAntiforgery()`.

## Troubleshooting 419

- Was the page loaded through the middleware? It sets the cookie.
- Does the cookie reach the browser? `Secure` cookies are dropped on plain HTTP; behind a TLS-terminating proxy, configure forwarded headers or set `CookieSecurePolicy.Always`.
- Do all instances share the Data Protection key ring?
- Does `UseAuthentication()` run before the antiforgery middleware?
- Did a sign-in or sign-out change the token? Reload the page, or use `OnRejected`.

See [Deploying](/docs/deploying) for proxy and multi-instance settings.

---

# Deploying behind a proxy

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/deploying

> Forwarded headers, secure cookies, compression, asset caching and multi-instance state.

Behind a load balancer or reverse proxy that terminates TLS, Kestrel sees plain HTTP unless the scheme is forwarded. Without it, the state and `XSRF-TOKEN` cookies are not marked `Secure`, and the version-mismatch `409` sends an `http://` `X-Inertia-Location`.

## Forwarded headers

```csharp
builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(o =>
{
    o.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
    // o.KnownProxies / o.KnownNetworks: list your proxy, or headers from anyone else are ignored
});

app.UseForwardedHeaders();               // first
app.UseInertia();
```

When the scheme cannot be forwarded, force the cookies:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.State.CookieSecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always);
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(o => o.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always);
```

## Multi-instance state

On several instances, share the Data Protection key ring so the state cookie and antiforgery tokens can be read by every instance:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddDataProtection()
    .PersistKeysToFileSystem(new DirectoryInfo("/var/keys"))
    .SetApplicationName("MyApp");
```

Using the session store? Sessions must be shared too (for example Redis). The default cookie store only needs shared Data Protection keys.

Keep the SSR server on loopback on each instance. See [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering).

## Compression

Page JSON and HTML compress five to ten times. Compress at the proxy, or in the app:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddResponseCompression();
app.UseResponseCompression();                // before UseStaticFiles and UseInertia
```

Over HTTPS the middleware compresses only with `o.EnableForHttps = true`. Review BREACH for your pages first: Inertia.Net keeps the antiforgery token in a cookie, not in the body, but a page that reflects request input next to a secret is still exposed.

## Asset caching

Vite puts a content hash in every built file name, so files under `build/assets` can be cached for good:

```csharp
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    OnPrepareResponse = c =>
    {
        if (c.Context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/build/assets"))
        {
            c.Context.Response.Headers.CacheControl = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
        }
    },
});
```

`app.MapStaticAssets()` does the same with build-time Brotli when the client is built before `dotnet publish`, so the files are in `wwwroot` when the static web assets manifest is generated.

## Path base

Use `app.UsePathBase("/app")` before `UseInertia()`. The page `url`, Vite URLs and `Back()` include the path base. If a proxy rewrites paths, set `o.UrlResolver` to return the browser-visible URL.

## Health and readiness

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddInertiaSsr();
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

The SSR health check is covered in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering#7-health-check).

## Deployment checklist

- [ ] The client `build` script runs before `dotnet publish` (`npm run build`, `bun run build`, `pnpm run build` or `yarn run build`), or `wwwroot/build` is copied into the publish output.
- [ ] `app.html` is copied to the publish output.
- [ ] Forwarded headers are configured, or cookies are forced secure.
- [ ] Data Protection keys are shared between instances.
- [ ] Static assets under `/build/assets` are cached as immutable.
- [ ] Response compression is enabled at the proxy or in the app.
- [ ] SSR listens on loopback and its bundle is deployed when SSR is enabled.
- [ ] The client build and server build are the same version, so `X-Inertia-Version` converges.

## Hosts and SSR failures

Keep `AllowedHosts` configured: an asset-version mismatch response includes the request URL. `Ssr.ConnectTimeout` bounds connection establishment (five seconds by default). In `SsrMode.Required`, the exception message is generic; diagnostic properties may contain private renderer details and should stay in trusted logs.

---

# Native AOT

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/native-aot

> Publish a Native AOT Inertia.Net app with source-generated JSON metadata.

`Inertia.Net`, `Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints` and `Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR` are annotated `IsAotCompatible`. A real app is published with Native AOT in CI (`tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke`) with zero trim and AOT warnings allowed. The library never reflects over your props: values are written with `JsonTypeInfo` from your `JsonSerializerContext`.

## 1. Register a JSON context

Register every prop type and chain the context into the HTTP JSON options:

```csharp
builder.Services.ConfigureHttpJsonOptions(o =>
    o.SerializerOptions.TypeInfoResolverChain.Insert(0, AppJsonContext.Default));

[JsonSerializable(typeof(UsersPage))]               // typed page props
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<UserDto>))]           // closed pagination types you return
[JsonSerializable(typeof(UserDto))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<UserDto>))]           // closed collection types you return
[JsonSerializable(typeof(UserDto[]))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Stats))]                   // the T of Defer(() => new Stats(...)) and friends
internal sealed partial class AppJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;
```

Register the type that each loader returns and each plain value you place in `InertiaProps`, plus flash values that are not plain strings or numbers. The library's own context already covers `string`, `bool`, `int`, `long`, `double`, `decimal`, `float`, `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `TimeSpan`, `JsonElement`, `string[]`, `int[]`, `List<string>`, `Dictionary<string, string>`, `Dictionary<string, string[]>`, `InertiaProps` and `Dictionary<string, object>`.

Members of type `InertiaProp` are accepted by the source generator without any attribute.

## 2. Make validation models public

The .NET 10 `AddValidation()` source generator skips internal types, and validation then silently does nothing. Only one `AddValidation()` call site per project is allowed.

## 3. Add ProblemDetails

```csharp
builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
```

The non-Inertia `400` validation problem needs the `ProblemDetails` JSON metadata, or it cannot be serialized without reflection.

## 4. Avoid anonymous types

Anonymous types do not work as props, flash values or published [live prop](/docs/live-props) values under AOT. Use `InertiaProps`, records or classes registered in the context, and register the types you publish as live values in the same context.

## 5. Copy content files

`app.html` and the Vite manifest are read from disk at runtime. Copy them to the publish directory, and set the content root to the binary's directory when it may run from elsewhere:

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateSlimBuilder(new WebApplicationOptions
{
    Args = args,
    ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory,
});
```

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <PublishAot>true</PublishAot>
  <JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault>false</JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault>
</PropertyGroup>
<ItemGroup>
  <Content Include="app.html" CopyToPublishDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## 6. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints

MVC is not AOT compatible (neither is MVC itself), so `Inertia.Net.Mvc` is not either. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints.

## 7. FastEndpoints source generation

```csharp
builder.Services.AddFastEndpoints(new[] { DiscoveredTypes.All });
```

`DiscoveredTypes` is generated by the `FastEndpoints.Generator` package, in the namespace named after the assembly. See `samples/FastEndpoints.Svelte`.

## 8. Trim HTTP/3

The SSR client never uses HTTP/3, so it can be trimmed out:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Net.SocketsHttpHandler.Http3Support" Value="false" Trim="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Cached props, the SSR cache, nonces, prefetching, `MapInertia`, the DevTools recorder and [live props over SignalR](/docs/live-props#signalr) are all AOT safe and covered by the smoke test. SignalR itself does not support strongly typed hubs (`Hub<T>`) under AOT, so keep any hubs of your own untyped.

<Callout type="tip" title="Catch missing registrations early">
Set `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false` in regular builds too. A missing `JsonSerializable` registration then fails in tests instead of only in the AOT publish.
</Callout>

The reference app is `tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke/Program.cs`. Run it end to end with `bash eng/aot-smoke.sh` on Linux with clang and zlib installed.

---

# Performance

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/performance

> Memory and hosting guidance, payload limits and the design choices behind the adapter.

Benchmarks cover page rendering, partial reloads, deferred props, SSR, caching and state storage. These controlled microbenchmarks are not production throughput estimates.

## Memory and hosting

The useful planning number is not a microbenchmark; it is how much memory the whole process needs at rest and under load. These are reference points measured on Linux x64 after the first request, not guarantees:

| App shape | RSS at rest | Plan for |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inertia.Net JIT app, no database (`samples/MinimalApi.React`) | about 90 MB | 256–512 MB |
| Inertia.Net Native AOT app (`tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke`) | about 42 MB | 128–256 MB |
| Small JIT todo: Minimal API + EF Core + SQLite + cookie auth | roughly 120–180 MB | 256–512 MB |
| Small Native AOT todo: source-generated JSON + SQLite | roughly 45–70 MB | 128–256 MB |
| Add managed Bun SSR | +30–60 MB for the Bun process | add 128 MB headroom |

The two Inertia.Net baseline rows were measured from this repository on Linux x64; the todo rows are planning ranges, not benchmark claims. The JIT todo range includes the runtime, EF Core, SQLite, authentication and a small working set. PostgreSQL or MongoDB, image processing and a large cache move it upward; measure your own app under realistic concurrency. Native AOT removes most JIT and reflection overhead, but it does not make EF Core or a database free.

For containers:

- Set a memory limit rather than relying on the host.
- Leave headroom for the GC, the OS page cache and request bursts.
- Expect SSR to add a second process. If the Bun renderer is optional, `SsrMode.Preferred` lets the app fall back to client rendering when it is unavailable.
- Profile with real page sizes. A dashboard with deferred props and a paginated feed behaves very differently from a page that serializes every row.

The benchmark project still has the throughput and allocation probes:

```sh
dotnet run -c Release --project tests/Inertia.Net.Benchmarks -- --filter '*'
```

Targeted probes: `--render-probe`, `--ssr-probe`, `--mvc-probe`, `--payload-probe` and `--cache-probe`.

## Payload size

The page JSON is fully buffered before the first byte is sent, so a failing loader never produces a half-written `200`. Each concurrent request therefore holds its whole page in memory (pooled, and sized from the component's recent pages).

Keep pages well under a megabyte:

- paginate with [`Scroll`](/docs/infinite-scroll)
- defer slow data with [`Defer`](/docs/deferred-props)
- load on demand with [`Optional`](/docs/props#the-prop-factories)
- use a [partial reload](/docs/partial-reloads) for refresh buttons and filters

`Ssr.MaxPageBytes` keeps larger pages off the SSR server and `Ssr.MaxResponseBytes` bounds its answer; neither limits the props.

## Design notes

- **Single pass.** One recursive walk filters props, runs loaders, writes JSON to a `Utf8JsonWriter` and collects the metadata. There is no intermediate object tree.
