- **Pooled buffers.** The page is written to a pooled `IBufferWriter<byte>`, and the path tracker is a pooled `char[]`. A path becomes a string only when metadata needs it.
- **Version check before the handler.** A stale client costs one header comparison and a `409`.
- **No per-request mutable singletons.** Per-request state lives in an `InertiaFeature` on `HttpContext.Features`, so concurrent requests cannot leak history or flash settings into one another.
- **Plain DTOs take the fast path.** A POCO, list or typed dictionary is walked only when its type can hold `InertiaProp` values (`InertiaProp`, `object` or dictionary members/elements; cached per type). Everything else is one `Serialize` call.
- **UTF-8 throughout.** SSR output and the MVC tag helpers write UTF-8 bytes; nothing large is materialized as a .NET string.
- **Cached assets.** The Vite manifest is parsed once, the root template is parsed once into pre-encoded UTF-8 segments, and the production tags are pre-rendered per entry set and path base. The version is a precomputed string compared ordinally. A missing manifest, template or SSR bundle is re-checked at most once per second.
- **Sync loaders stay sync.** `Func<T>` loaders are not wrapped in closures.

Most per-request allocation in a real handler is the props you build, not the render.

## Paired render measurements

Warm, in-process probes on .NET 10 compared 32 alternating rounds in two runs. Times are medians of within-round ratios; B/op values are from run 2.

| Workload | Before B/op | After B/op | Run 1 paired time | Run 2 paired time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| JSON, 20 mixed props | 1,736 | 1,736 | −1.6% | −0.6% |
| Integer-key dictionary, 1,000 props | 176,592 | 166,688 | −52.2% | −53.7% |
| GUID-key dictionary, 500 rows | 140,712 | 140,304 | −28.5% | −33.0% |
| Eight scroll props, append wrappers | 6,664 | 6,088 | −2.2% | −3.4% |
| Eight scroll props, prepend wrappers | 6,880 | 6,112 | −6.2% | −5.4% |

These synthetic measurements do not establish HTTP throughput or general latency. Pooled entries grow from 24 to 32 bytes, so warm savings do not imply a smaller cold or concurrent pool footprint. Full methods, controls and rejected candidates are in [benchmark results](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/tests/Inertia.Net.Benchmarks/RESULTS.md).

Parallel prop planning and DevTools recording each use a process-wide latch that remains active after first use. Measure with the features used by your own app.

---

# Multiple apps and libraries

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/mounts

> Mount a second Inertia UI under its own path, with its own shared props, asset version, state cookie, root view, error pages and SSR.

One ASP.NET Core app can serve more than one Inertia UI. A typical case is a library, such as an admin dashboard, that ships
its own prebuilt client and is mounted under `/dashboard` in a host app that already uses Inertia.Net.

Each UI is a **mount**: a named `InertiaOptions` that `app.UseInertia(name)` selects inside an `app.Map(...)` branch. The
default mount is the one `AddInertia(...)` and `UseInertia()` configure, so existing apps do not change.

## What a mount keeps to itself

| Per mount | Shared by all mounts |
|---|---|
| Shared props (`o.Share`) and every other `InertiaOptions` setting | `IInertiaCache` and the cache store (choose distinct `InertiaProp.Cache(key)` keys) |
| Asset version: the 409 check only compares against the mount's own version | `IInertiaLive` and the SignalR hub |
| State cookie: `.Inertia.State.{name}` and `.Inertia.Previous.{name}` by default | Metrics (named mounts add an `inertia.mount` tag) and DevTools |
| Root view: the mount's `RootView` file, or a keyed `IInertiaRootView` | Antiforgery and data protection |
| Vite manifest, SSR servers, managed Node processes, TypeScript output | The SSR `HttpClient` (its `ConnectTimeout` comes from the default mount) |
| Error pages registered with `AddInertiaErrorPages(name, ...)` | |

## Register and map a mount

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.Share("user", ctx => ctx.User.Identity?.Name)); // the host app

builder.Services.AddInertia("dashboard", o =>
{
    o.Version = "dashboard-2.1.0";          // the dashboard's own asset version
    o.RootView = "dashboard.html";           // or register a keyed IInertiaRootView, below
    o.Share("product", "Dashboard");
});

var app = builder.Build();

app.Map("/dashboard", dashboard =>
{
    dashboard.UseInertia("dashboard");       // before routing in the branch
    dashboard.UseRouting();
    dashboard.UseEndpoints(e => e.MapGet("/", () => Render("Dashboard/Index")));
});

app.UseInertia();                            // the host app's mount
app.MapGet("/", () => Render("Home"));
```

`Map` sets the request's path base, so page URLs, `Back()` fallbacks, Vite asset URLs and the previous-URL cookie stay inside
`/dashboard`. Calling `AddInertia("dashboard", ...)` again adds to that mount's configuration.

Startup fails when `UseInertia(name)` names a mount that was never registered, or when two mounts share a state or
previous-URL cookie name.

## A root view shipped by a library

A library cannot rely on a file in the host's content root. Register a keyed `IInertiaRootView` that writes an embedded
template instead:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddKeyedSingleton<IInertiaRootView, DashboardRootView>("dashboard");

sealed class DashboardRootView : IInertiaRootView
{
    public async ValueTask RenderAsync(InertiaRootViewContext context)
    {
        var html = context.HttpContext.Response;
        await html.WriteAsync("<!doctype html><html><head><script type=\"module\" src=\"/dashboard/app.js\"></script></head><body>");
        await html.WriteAsync(context.GetBodyHtml()); // the page script and root element
        await html.WriteAsync("</body></html>");
    }
}
```

## Error pages per mount

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaErrorPages();                                         // the host's Error component
builder.Services.AddInertiaErrorPages("dashboard", o => o.Component = "Dashboard/Error");

app.UseInertiaErrorPages();                                                      // once, before the Map branches
```

A mount renders only the error components registered for it, because another mount's components are not in its bundle. A
mount without `AddInertiaErrorPages(name, ...)` leaves its errors to the rest of the pipeline.

## SSR, health checks and TypeScript

Each mount has its own SSR gateway, and its own managed Node processes when `o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess()` is set; give each mount
its own `BasePort`. Check a mount's SSR servers with:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddInertiaSsrForMount("dashboard"); // named "inertia-ssr-dashboard"
```

`o.TypeScript.OutputPath` is per mount too, so each client gets its own generated declarations.

## For library authors

Expose one registration call and one mapping call, and keep the mount name private to the library:

```csharp
public static IServiceCollection AddDashboard(this IServiceCollection services) =>
    services.AddInertia("dashboard", o => o.Version = DashboardAssets.Version)
            .AddKeyedSingleton<IInertiaRootView, DashboardRootView>("dashboard");

public static IApplicationBuilder MapDashboard(this IApplicationBuilder app, string path) =>
    app.Map(path, branch =>
    {
        branch.UseInertia("dashboard");
        branch.UseRouting();
        branch.UseEndpoints(e => { /* the dashboard's endpoints */ });
    });
```

Mounts are adapter configuration: the Inertia protocol on the wire does not change.

---

# Configuration

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/configuration

> InertiaOptions, Vite, SSR, props, state and the middleware and result API.

Core configuration is passed to `AddInertia`; error page options use `AddInertiaErrorPages`. Options marked “Development only” do nothing in other environments.

## `AddInertia(o => ...)`: `InertiaOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RootView` | `"app.html"` | Root template relative to the content root (a Razor view name with `UseRazorRootView`). Paths outside the content root are refused. |
| `RootElementId` | `"app"` | Id of the root element and the `data-page` script. |
| `Version` | `null` | Asset version. `null` means the Vite manifest hash, or `""` without one. |
| `VersionResolver` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string?>` per-request version; wins over `Version` when non-null. |
| `EncryptHistory` | `false` | Encrypt browser history state of every page. |
| `WithAllErrors` | `false` | Send every validation message per field instead of the first. |
| `PreserveBigIntegers` | `false` | Emit integers beyond ±(2^53−1) as `{"$bigint":"..."}`. |
| `ExposeSharedPropKeys` | `true` | List top-level shared keys in `sharedProps`. |
| `CspNonce` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string?>`: the request's CSP nonce. |
| `ConvertExternalRedirects` | `true` | Turn an Inertia redirect to another origin into `409` + `X-Inertia-Location`. |
| `UrlResolver` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string>`: the page `url`. |
| `Pages.Directory` / `Pages.Extensions` | `null` / `.tsx .jsx .ts .js .vue .svelte` | Development check that a rendered component has a page file. |
| `TypeScript.OutputPath`, `.Page<T>(component)`, `.SharedProps<T>()`, `.FlashData<T>()` | `null` | TypeScript declarations, written in Development. |
| `Share(key, value)` / `Share(key, Func<HttpContext, object?>)` | none | Shared props. |

## `o.Pagination`: `PaginationOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DefaultPerPage` | `20` | Default page size. |
| `MaxPerPage` | `100` | Maximum page size (below `int.MaxValue` to allow over-fetching); the default must be between 1 and this value. |
| `PageName` | `"page"` | Numbered-page query parameter. |
| `PerPageName` | `"perPage"` | Page-size query parameter. |
| `CursorName` | `"cursor"` | Cursor query parameter. |

## `o.Vite`: `ViteOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PublicDirectory` | `"wwwroot"` | Web root containing the build directory and hot file. |
| `BuildDirectory` | `"build"` | Vite output directory under `PublicDirectory`; also the URL prefix. |
| `ManifestPath` | `null` | Manifest path relative to the content root. `null` = `{PublicDirectory}/{BuildDirectory}/.vite/manifest.json`, then `manifest.json`. |
| `HotFilePath` | `null` | Hot file relative to the content root. `null` = `{PublicDirectory}/hot`. Read in Development only. |
| `DevServerUrl` | `null` | Dev server origin, e.g. `http://localhost:5173`. When set, dev tags always render. |
| `AssetBaseUrl` | `null` | Replaces `{PathBase}/{BuildDirectory}` as the URL prefix of built assets. |
| `Prefetch` | `None` | `Waterfall` or `Aggressive`: prefetch code-split chunks after load. |
| `PrefetchConcurrency` | `3` | Chunks `Waterfall` downloads at a time. |

## `o.Ssr`: `SsrOptions`

`Ssr.ConnectTimeout` bounds connection establishment separately from the rendering deadline and defaults to five seconds; use a positive supported duration or `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Mode` | `Disabled` | `Disabled`, `Preferred` or `Required`. `Disabled` cannot be overridden per response. |
| `Urls` | empty (`http://127.0.0.1:13714`) | SSR server base URLs. Not used with `UseNodeProcess()`. |
| `Timeout` | `5 s` | Total deadline per render. `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` disables it. |
| `MaxResponseBytes` | `16 MiB` | Limit on actual response bytes, including errors and chunked responses. |
| `MaxPageBytes` | `2 MiB` | Pages whose JSON is larger render on the client without a call. |
| `BundlePath` | `null` | Skip SSR while this file is missing, unless the Vite dev server runs. |
| `ExcludePaths` | empty | Request paths never rendered on the server (exact, or a trailing `*` for a prefix). |
| `Concurrency.MaxActive` | `8` | Renders in flight per server from this app instance; `0` for no limit. |
| `Concurrency.MaxQueued` | `32` | Renders waiting for a slot per server. |
| `Concurrency.QueueTimeout` | `250 ms` | How long a render waits for a slot. |
| `CircuitBreaker.Enabled` | `true` | Pause servers that keep failing. |
| `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` | `5` | Consecutive failures that open a server's circuit. |
| `CircuitBreaker.BreakDuration` | `10 s` | How long an open circuit skips the server before one probe. |
| `Cache.Duration` | `Zero` (off) | Reuse a render for this long when the page JSON is the same. |
| `Cache.StaleFor` | `Zero` | Serve stale while re-rendering. |
| `Cache.MaxBytes` | `64 MiB` | Size of the default store's render cache. |
| `UseNodeProcess(configure?)` | off | Start and supervise Node SSR processes (sets `Mode = Preferred` when `Disabled`). |

Per response: `Render(...).WithSsr(SsrMode)` and `.WithoutSsr()`. The full SSR options are in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering).

## `o.Props`: `InertiaPropsOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MaxConcurrency` | `4` | Loaders marked `.Parallel()` that run at once per render. Must be positive. |

## `o.State`: `InertiaStateOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CookieName` | `".Inertia.State"` | Cookie name (cookie store) or session key (session store). |
| `RememberPreviousUrl` | `false` | Remember successful page GET URLs for `Back()` when Referer is unavailable. |
| `PreviousUrlCookieName` | `".Inertia.Previous"` | Plain previous-URL cookie, with either state store; non-empty and different from `CookieName`. |
| `CookieSecurePolicy` | `SameAsRequest` | When state and previous-URL cookies are `Secure`. |
| `UseSession()` | off | Use `ISession` instead of the encrypted cookie. |
| `AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseTempDataStateStore())` | off | Use MVC TempData. Inertia.Net.Mvc package. |

## `AddInertiaErrorPages(o => ...)`: `InertiaErrorPagesOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Component` | `"Error"` | Default error component. |
| `Components` | empty | Per-status overrides, with keys in `StatusCodes`. |
| `StatusCodes` | `[403, 404, 500, 503]` | Non-empty set of statuses from 400–599. Protocol `409` and antiforgery `419` responses are preserved. |
| `EnabledInDevelopment` | `false` | Preview error components in Development. |
| `Props` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, int, Exception?, InertiaProps>` for additional props. |

See [Error pages](/docs/error-pages) for setup, shared props and existing exception middleware.

## Middleware and endpoint API

| API | Description |
|---|---|
| `services.AddInertia(configure?)` | Registers services and options. |
| `services.AddInertiaErrorPages(configure?)` / `app.UseInertiaErrorPages(useExceptionHandler: true)` | Error page services and middleware, before `UseInertia()`. Use `false` with your own `UseExceptionHandler()`. |
| `app.UseInertia()` | The protocol middleware. Before the endpoints; after `UseSession()` when used. |
| `app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(configure?)` | Issues the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and validates unsafe requests (`419` on failure). |
| `app.MapInertia(pattern, component, props?)` | GET and HEAD endpoint that renders the component. |
| `services.AddInertiaDevTools(configure?)` / `app.MapInertiaDevTools()` | DevTools recorder and read API. A warning is logged when recording is enabled outside Development without an `Authorize` callback; the read API then returns 404. |
| `app.UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN")` | Only writes the token cookie; validation is up to you. |
| `endpoint.WithInertiaValidation()` | Minimal API: validation failures redirect back with errors. |
| `endpoint.WithInertiaPrecognition()` | Minimal API: `WithInertiaValidation()` plus Precognition. |
| `healthChecks.AddInertiaSsr(...)` | SSR health check from the gateway's state. |
| `mvc.AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseRazorRootView("App"))` | MVC filter, optional Razor root view and component resolver. |
| `config.ConfigureInertia(configure?)` | FastEndpoints: validation redirect and Precognition. |
| `Render(component, props?)` | `InertiaResult`: `.WithStatusCode`, `.WithRootView`, `.WithViewData`, `.WithSsr`, `.WithoutSsr`, `.WithSsrCache`. |
| `Location(url)` | `InertiaLocationResult`. |
| `Back(fallback = "~/")` | `InertiaBackResult`: `.WithErrors`, `.WithFlash`. |
| `httpContext.Inertia()` | `InertiaFeature`: `Share`, `Flash`, `WithErrors`, `ClearHistory`, `EncryptHistory`, `PreserveFragment`. |
| `Send.InertiaAsync(...)`, `Send.InertiaLocationAsync(...)`, `Send.InertiaBackAsync(...)` | FastEndpoints `Send` extensions. |

## Extension points

`IInertiaRootView`, `IInertiaStateStore`, `ViteAssets`, `InertiaRequest` (parsed headers), `InertiaHeaders` (header name constants), `InertiaSsrException`, `InertiaSsr.HttpClientName` (the SSR HTTP client) and `InertiaDiagnostics` (meter and activity source names).

## Name collisions

The package imports `Inertia.Net` and static members of `Inertia.Net.Inertia` when implicit usings are enabled. If a name such as `Location` collides with a type, use `Inertia.Net.Inertia.Location(url)`. To manage imports yourself, set `<InertiaNetImplicitUsings>false</InertiaNetImplicitUsings>` in the project and add `using Inertia.Net;` and `using static Inertia.Net.Inertia;` where needed.

`InertiaPropJsonConverter`, `InertiaSsrHealthCheck`, `InertiaCacheEntryKind`, `InertiaCacheEntryOptions`, `InertiaPagesOptions`, `InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(...)` and `InertiaPrecognitionMetadata` are public APIs for serialization, health checks, cache stores, page checks and precognitive request handling.

---

# TypeScript types

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/typescript

> Generate declarations for page props, shared props and flash data from your .NET contracts.

Inertia.Net can write TypeScript declarations for typed page props, shared props and flash data. They follow the app's JSON contracts (the HTTP JSON options and their source-generated contexts), so names, nullability and enum values match the page JSON.

## Configure generation

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.TypeScript.OutputPath = "ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts";   // written in Development, only when it changed
    o.TypeScript.Page<UsersPage>("Users/Index").Page<HomePage>("Home");
    o.TypeScript.FlashData<Flash>();                             // optional; SharedProps<T>() too
});

public sealed record UsersPage(
    List<User> Users,
    [property: InertiaPropType(typeof(UserStats))] InertiaProp Stats);
```

The file is written when the app starts in Development, and only when its content changed. Commit it so `tsc` passes in CI without running the app.

```ts
// ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts (excerpt)
export interface InertiaPages {
  'Users/Index': UsersPage
  Home: HomePage
}
export interface UsersPage {
  users: User[]
  stats?: UserStats
}
declare module '@inertiajs/core' {
  export interface InertiaConfig {
    sharedPageProps: SharedProps
    flashDataType: FlashData
    errorValueType: string
  }
}
```

```tsx
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'

export default function Index({ users, stats }: InertiaPages['Users/Index']) {
  // ...
}
```

## Shared props

Shared props are inferred from the values passed to `o.Share(...)`; dot keys nest. Factories and per-request shares are typed as `unknown`. `o.TypeScript.SharedProps<T>()` replaces the inference with an explicit type. The `InertiaConfig` augmentation types `usePage().props` and `flash`.

## Prop members

An `InertiaProp` member is optional (it can be deferred, optional or rescued) and `unknown`, unless `[InertiaPropType(typeof(T))]` names its value type.

## Mapping

| .NET | TypeScript |
|---|---|
| `int`, `long`, `double`, `decimal`, `float` | `number` (`number \| bigint` for 64-bit and larger with `PreserveBigIntegers`) |
| `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `Guid`, `byte[]` | `string` |
| enum | union of JSON values (string names with a string enum converter) |
| dictionary | `Record<string, T>` |
| polymorphic type | union tagged with its discriminator |
| nullable member | `T \| null` |

Types missing from the JSON metadata (under Native AOT, register them in your context) are `unknown`, with a warning in the log.

Number handling follows member settings, then type settings, then the global JSON options. Custom converter output is typed as `unknown` with a warning when its shape cannot be inferred.

<Callout type="info" title="Validation and JSON names">
Props and MVC validation error keys use the HTTP `JsonOptions`. FastEndpoints error keys use its binding serializer policy. Keep client field names aligned with the applicable policy; custom resolvers without member metadata may require client JSON names for aliases.
</Callout>

---

# Testing

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/testing

> Fluent assertions over Inertia responses and helpers for partial reloads and deferred props.

`Inertia.Net.Testing` has Laravel-style fluent assertions over Inertia responses and `HttpClient` helpers. It parses both JSON responses (`X-Inertia: true`) and the first-visit HTML `<script data-page>`, and decodes `$bigint` values. Failures throw `InertiaAssertionException` with a readable message, so it works with any test framework.

```csharp
using Inertia.Net.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;

public class UsersTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory) : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    // Keeps cookies (flash, errors) and does not follow redirects, so a test can assert the 303 itself.
    private readonly HttpClient _client = factory.CreateClient(new WebApplicationFactoryClientOptions
    {
        AllowAutoRedirect = false,
    });

    [Fact]
    public async Task Index_lists_users()
    {
        using var response = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users");   // sends X-Inertia, X-Requested-With

        await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page
            .Component("Users/Index")
            .Url("/users")
            .Has("users", 3, first => first.Where("name", "Ann").WhereType("id", "integer").Etc())
            .Where("filters.search", "")
            .Missing("secret")
            .HasFlash("toast", "Welcome"));
    }
}
```

Add `public partial class Program;` to your app when it uses top-level statements.

To check that an error page keeps its HTTP status, use `Status` with the response's page assertion:

```csharp
using var response = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/missing");
await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page.Status(404).Component("Error"));
```

## Request helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `InertiaGetAsync(url, version?, configure?)` | Sends an Inertia GET |
| `InertiaRequestAsync(method, url, content?, version?, configure?)` | Sends an Inertia request with any method |
| `GetInertiaPageAsync()` | Parses the response into an `InertiaPage` |
| `AssertInertiaAsync(assert)` | Parses, runs the assertions and returns the page |

## Page assertions

`Component`, `Url`, `Version`, `HasFlash(key)`, `HasFlash(key, value)`, `MissingFlash(key)`, `HasDeferred(path)`, `HasDeferred(group, path)`, `HasLive(path)` and `HasLive(path, channel, event)` for [live props](/docs/live-props) (the channel as `"{type}:{name}"`, e.g. `private:orders.1`).

## Prop assertions

On props and nested scopes (dot paths and array indexes allowed):

`Has(key)`, `Has(key, count)`, `Has(key, scope)`, `Has(key, count, firstItemScope)`, `HasAll`, `HasAny`, `Missing`, `MissingAll`, `Where(key, value)`, `Where(key, predicate)`, `WhereNot`, `WhereNull`, `WhereNotNull`, `WhereType(key, "string|null")`, `WhereAllType`, `WhereContains(key, ...)`, `Count`, `CountBetween`, `Each(scope)`, `First(scope)` and `Dump()`.

**Strict interaction tracking.** Like Laravel, a nested scope fails when it contains properties you did not assert, unless you end it with `Etc()`. The root scope is not checked automatically: call `.Interacted()` at the end to enforce that every top-level prop was asserted.

## Partial reloads and deferred props

`InertiaPage` replays the request with the right headers:

```csharp
var page = await (await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

new AssertableInertia(page).HasDeferred("sidebar", "stats").Missing("stats");

var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(_client, "sidebar");     // all groups when none are named
new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("stats");

new AssertableInertia(page).HasScroll("posts");
var next = await page.LoadNextPageAsync(_client, "posts");
var previous = await next.LoadPreviousPageAsync(_client, "posts");

var only = await page.ReloadOnlyAsync(_client, "users");
var except = await page.ReloadExceptAsync(_client, "users");
```

`HasScroll(path)` asserts scroll metadata; `HasScroll(path, currentPage, nextPage)` also checks the page values. The page helpers use the metadata and send the appropriate append or prepend intent.

`ReloadOnlyAsync` asserts that `"users"` is in the result; `ReloadExceptAsync` asserts that it is missing.

## InertiaPage members

`Props`, `Raw`, `Prop(path)`, `HasProp(path)`, `PropBigInteger(path)`, `DeferredProps`, `MergeProps`, `PrependProps`, `DeepMergeProps`, `MatchPropsOn`, `RescuedProps`, `SharedProps`, `ScrollProps`, `OnceProps`, `LiveProps`, `Flash`, `EncryptHistory`, `ClearHistory`, `PreserveFragment`, `PreserveBigIntegers`.

<Callout type="tip" title="Cookies and redirects">
Flash and errors travel in a cookie across the redirect, so use a client that keeps cookies. Disable `AllowAutoRedirect` to assert the redirect itself, then follow it with a second `InertiaGetAsync` to read the flash or errors.
</Callout>

## Testing a form with antiforgery

Keep cookies and disable redirects on the test client. Load the form first, then send its XSRF token on the Inertia POST and follow the redirect:

```csharp
using var formPage = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users/create");
using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/users")
{
    Content = JsonContent.Create(new { email = "" }),
};
request.Headers.Add("X-Inertia", "true");
request.Headers.Add("X-Requested-With", "XMLHttpRequest");
request.Headers.Referrer = new Uri(_client.BaseAddress!, "/users/create");
request.WithXsrfToken(formPage);
using var response = await _client.SendAsync(request);
Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Redirect, response.StatusCode);
using var redirected = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users/create");
await redirected.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page.HasErrors().HasError("email"));
```

Import `System.Net` and `System.Net.Http.Json`. For a named bag use `HasErrorBag("createUser")` and `HasError("email", bag: "createUser")`. Dotted keys such as `items.0.email` are matched as flat error keys; with all errors enabled a message assertion matches any message. `GetXsrfToken()` and `WithXsrfToken()` accept custom cookie and header names. The cookie container must retain the antiforgery cookie as well as the Inertia state cookie.

---

# DevTools

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/devtools

> Record visits for the Inertia DevTools extension and catch missing page components during development.

The [Inertia DevTools](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/advanced/devtools) browser extension shows every visit, its props, headers and page state. Inertia.Net implements the server protocol.

## Enable DevTools

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaDevTools();   // records in Development only
app.UseInertia();
app.MapInertiaDevTools();                // GET /_inertia/devtools/entries/{id} and /entries
```

Each request through `UseInertia()` gets an `X-Inertia-Devtools-Id` and an entry in memory (per browser tab, at most `MaxEntriesPerTab` and `MaxEntries`, for `MaxAge`): request type, timings, headers, bodies, the page object and its props metadata.

The first page carries the discovery tag the extension reads. Values of names containing `password`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `api_key` are replaced with `[REDACTED]` in props, bodies and headers. Add names with `RedactedKeys`. Nothing leaves the app.

Sensitive query parameters are also redacted in recorded request/page URLs, redirects and URL headers; actual application URLs are unchanged. Malformed JSON bodies are omitted. Only eligible Inertia text bodies with a known length up to `MaxBodyBytes` are buffered; unknown-length nonseekable bodies are omitted as streamed, so recording does not spool bulk requests to disk.

Outside Development nothing is recorded unless `Enabled = true`, and the read API answers only requests that `Authorize` accepts (`404` otherwise). With `Pages.Directory` set, entries link the component to its file.

## Page component check

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Pages.Directory = "ClientApp/pages";   // Development only
    o.Pages.Extensions = [".tsx", ".vue"];   // optional
});
```

In Development, `Render` throws when the component has no page file, naming the closest one:

```text
'Users/Indx' was not found in 'ClientApp/pages' ... Did you mean 'Users/Index'?
```

Names match exactly, as the client resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems. Outside Development there is no check and no file access.

`Pages.Extensions` lists the file types: `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.vue` and `.svelte` by default.

## Generated TypeScript

The development startup also writes TypeScript declarations when `o.TypeScript.OutputPath` is set. It only writes the file when the content changed. See [TypeScript types](/docs/typescript).

## What to check before deploying

- `Pages.Directory` can stay configured; it is inactive outside Development.
- DevTools recording is off unless explicitly enabled.
- The generated TypeScript file is committed if the client build type-checks in CI.
- Production logs do not contain the DevTools read API.

<Callout type="tip" title="Pair with the browser extension">
Install the Inertia DevTools extension, open your app in Development, and use the extension's panel. The server entries are correlated by the `X-Inertia-Devtools-Id` header.
</Callout>

If recording is enabled outside Development without an `Authorize` callback, the app logs a warning and the read API returns 404. Map the reader with `MapInertiaDevTools()` and authorize its users. The recorder's process-wide latch remains active once used; parallel-prop planning also uses a process-wide latch after its first use.

---

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/troubleshooting

> Common errors, their causes, and how to fix them.

## `Inertia.Render(...)` does not compile

`'Inertia' is a namespace`. Call `Render(...)` unqualified. The namespace `Inertia.Net` shadows the class name outside the `Inertia.Net` namespace.

The global usings come from the package's `buildTransitive` props and need `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`. Without implicit usings, or with `InertiaNetImplicitUsings` set to `false`, add `using static Inertia.Net.Inertia;`.

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem title="Generated code fails with 'Inertia' is a type">
    Inside a namespace that starts with `Inertia.Net.`, the name `Inertia` binds to the `Inertia.Net.Inertia` class. Source generators that emit non-`global::` names starting with `Inertia` then break. Do not put your app's code under an `Inertia.Net.*` namespace.
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Vite manifest not found. Looked in: ...">
    Run your package manager’s build script (`npm run build`, `bun run build`, `pnpm run build` or `yarn run build`), or start the dev server so the hot file exists in Development, or set `o.Vite.ManifestPath` / `o.Vite.BuildDirectory`. Check that Vite writes `.vite/manifest.json` (`build.manifest: true`, Vite 5 and later) to `wwwroot/build`, and that the build output is part of what you deploy.
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Vite entry '...' was not found in the manifest">
    The `@vite("...")` argument must equal the manifest key, which is the path relative to the Vite root. The error lists the available entries.
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

## My 404 shows the Inertia modal in production

Register `AddInertiaErrorPages()` and call `UseInertiaErrorPages()` before `UseInertia()`. Create your error components; see [Error pages](/docs/error-pages).

## Form submissions fail with 419

`UseInertiaAntiforgery()` rejected a request without a valid `X-XSRF-TOKEN`. Check that:

- the page was loaded through the middleware (it sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie);
- the cookie reaches the browser (`Secure` on plain HTTP is dropped; see [Deploying](/docs/deploying));
- all instances share the Data Protection key ring;
- `UseAuthentication()` runs before it.

A sign-in or sign-out changes the token: reload the page, or return `Back()` from `OnRejected`. Exempt webhooks and token-authenticated APIs with `.DisableAntiforgery()` or `ShouldValidate`.

## The Inertia page component was not found

`o.Pages.Directory` is set and the component passed to `Render(...)` has no page file there. Names match exactly, as the client's page resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems; the message suggests the closest page. Fix the name, or check `Pages.Extensions` when your pages use another extension. The check never runs outside Development.

## A redirect to another site turns into a 409

That is `ConvertExternalRedirects` (on by default): an Inertia request cannot follow a redirect to another origin, so it gets `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` and the client does a full visit.

If it happens for your own host, the app is behind a proxy that does not forward the scheme (see [Deploying](/docs/deploying)), or use relative redirects. `o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false` disables the conversion.

## The root view resolves outside the content root

`RootView` and `WithRootView(...)` take a path relative to the content root; absolute paths and `..` are refused. Never derive them from request data.

## The page keeps reloading, or a request loops with 409

A `409` means the asset version differs between the client and the server. A loop means it never converges: usually the version changes on every request (a `VersionResolver` that returns a new value each time, or a manifest regenerated by a file watcher), or different instances behind a load balancer serve different builds. Use a stable version string.

In Development the manifest hash changes after each `vite build`, which is expected once.

## A blank page at localhost:5173

`http://localhost:5173` is the Vite dev server. It serves assets and hot-reload updates to your app and has no pages of its own, so it shows a blank page. Open the ASP.NET Core URL printed by `dotnet watch` or `dotnet run` instead (`http://localhost:5180` in the starter templates).

## The dev server tags do not appear

The hot file is read only when `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`. Check that `wwwroot/hot` exists and contains `http://localhost:5173`, or set `o.Vite.DevServerUrl`. Remember `base: '/'` for the dev server in `vite.config`.

## The root template was not found, or @inertia is missing

`RootView` is relative to the **content root**. Copy `app.html` to the output and publish directories (`CopyToOutputDirectory`, `CopyToPublishDirectory`). The template must contain `@inertia`.

## Flash data or errors disappear

The state cookie is limited to about 4 KB by browsers. Flash less data, or use `o.State.UseSession()`. If the app runs on several instances, share Data Protection keys.

If the cookie is never sent back, check the cookie `Secure` flag on HTTP behind a proxy that does not forward `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

## Validation errors do not show up (Minimal API)

Use `.WithInertiaValidation()` on the endpoint. Without it, the built-in `AddValidation()` filter returns a `400` problem details that the Inertia client cannot use. Make sure the model types are `public`.

## Validation keys do not match my field names

Keys use dotted indices and available JSON member aliases. Minimal API and MVC use the page serializer’s HTTP JSON options and FastEndpoints its binding serializer policy; keep these aligned with client field names. Metadata-free or custom resolver paths can fall back to naming-policy conversion. See [Validation](/docs/validation-and-errors).

## InertiaProp values can only be serialized by Inertia.Net

An `InertiaProp` ended up somewhere Inertia.Net does not walk: a `Flash(...)` value, a read-only dictionary type that does not implement `IDictionary`, or a type with a custom converter.

Lists, typed dictionaries (`Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` with any key type), `object` members and `IDictionary<string, object?>` are walked. Put props in `InertiaProps`, or declare the member as `InertiaProp` (or `object`) on the typed page object.

## Native AOT: JsonTypeInfo metadata was not provided

Add the type to your `JsonSerializerContext` and chain it with `ConfigureHttpJsonOptions`. Setting `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false` in regular builds finds these early. See [Native AOT](/docs/native-aot).

## SSR does not run and there is no error

SSR falls back to client rendering on any failure. Look for the warnings `Inertia SSR failed (...)` and `Inertia SSR skipped (...)`. The first includes the server's hint.

Check `o.Ssr.Mode`, `Urls`, that the Node server is running (`GET /health`; with `UseNodeProcess()` look for `Inertia.Net.Ssr` log lines), that `BundlePath` points at the built file, that the path is not in `ExcludePaths`, and that the page is under `MaxPageBytes`.

Set `Mode = SsrMode.Required` in Development to surface the failure.

## SSR skipped (circuit-open) or (overloaded)

- `circuit-open`: the server failed `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` times in a row and is skipped for `BreakDuration`; the earlier `Inertia SSR failed` warnings say why.
- `overloaded`: more renders arrived than `Concurrency.MaxActive` plus `MaxQueued`, or one waited longer than `QueueTimeout`. Add servers or instances, or raise the limits if the server has headroom.

## Several managed instances never become healthy

Every instance must listen on its own port: the SSR entry has to read `process.env.INERTIA_SSR_PORT`. A bundle built only by `@inertiajs/vite` listens on its baked-in port.

## The SSR output is not hydrated

Use the hydrating client entry shown in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering) and build both bundles from the same sources. The SSR body is marked `data-server-rendered="true"`.

## Does it work behind a path base?

Yes. The page `url` keeps the path base, the Vite URLs include it, and `Back()` works.

## Can I use Newtonsoft.Json?

No. Props use System.Text.Json with the HTTP JSON options.

## Can I mix Razor Pages or views with Inertia pages?

Yes. Inertia handles only the endpoints that return `Render(...)`. The middleware leaves other responses alone, apart from `Vary: X-Inertia`.

## Forms submit invalid data

Minimal API endpoints need `.WithInertiaValidation()` or `.WithInertiaPrecognition()` and `AddValidation()`. Endpoint construction throws when validation resolvers are missing; routing can construct endpoints lazily. See [Validation](/docs/validation-and-errors).

## 419 in tests

Use a cookie-preserving client, load an Inertia page first, then use `request.WithXsrfToken(pageResponse)` on the form request. See [Testing](/docs/testing#testing-a-form-with-antiforgery).

## Precognition: login locks users out while typing

Precognitive POSTs pass through rate limiting. Use separate bounded validation and submission partitions and validate on blur; see [Precognition](/docs/precognition#rate-limiting). A throttled validation still rejects, so show a retry message. To render a custom Inertia error page for a real submission rejected with 429, add 429 with `AddInertiaErrorPages(o => o.StatusCodes.Add(429))` and put `UseInertiaErrorPages()` before `UseRateLimiter()`. Precognitive JSON responses keep their 429 and `Precognition: true` header.

## 'Location' is a type but is used like a variable

The imported static `Location` name may collide with a type. Call `Inertia.Net.Inertia.Location(url)` explicitly, or opt out with `<InertiaNetImplicitUsings>false</InertiaNetImplicitUsings>` and add your own imports. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration#name-collisions).

## A cached prop loader runs every request

Check that the key and duration are stable and the cache store works. Dot-key props support caching; include every user or tenant dependency in the cache key. A stale refresh needs its own scope and may be dropped when the background queue is full. See [Props](/docs/props#cached-props).

---

# Build a todo app

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/forget-me-not

> Build a complete Inertia.Net todo app with session login, public lists, paginated loading, reminders and SSR.

ForgetMeNot is a small todo app, but it uses the same pieces as a real product: sign-in, private data, a public share page, a list that loads as you scroll, and reminders that run in the background. You will start from the official `Inertia.Net.Templates` template, then add each feature one small step at a time.

<Callout type="info" title="What you need">
- .NET 10 SDK
- JavaScript tooling with npm, Bun, pnpm or Yarn
- A code editor
- A terminal

No database server is required. ForgetMeNot uses SQLite, and the template already gives you a working React app.
</Callout>

Commands below use Bun; npm, pnpm and Yarn work as alternatives. The production example uses Bun as its SSR runtime.

This guide is for someone who has not built an Inertia app before. Run the commands, look at the checkpoints, and only move on when the app behaves the way the checkpoint says.

## What you are building

<Cards>
  <Card title="Sign in with sessions" icon="shield">Register, sign in, sign out and keep flash messages in the same session.</Card>
  <Card title="Private todo lists" icon="book">Create lists, add items, mark them done and set due dates.</Card>
  <Card title="Public share pages" icon="sparkles">Share an unguessable URL that opens without an account.</Card>
  <Card title="Virtual loading" icon="code">Load todo items in pages with `Scroll` and `InfiniteScroll`.</Card>
  <Card title="Reminders" icon="gauge">Set a reminder time and let a background worker send it once.</Card>
  <Card title="Pretty UI" icon="blocks">Use Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui components instead of inline styles.</Card>
</Cards>

## 1. Start from the template

Install the templates once, then create the app:

```sh
dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates::1.7.0
dotnet new inertia -n ForgetMeNot --framework react
cd ForgetMeNot
bun install
```

For npm, pnpm or Yarn, use `npm install`, `pnpm install` or `yarn install`. Start the two development processes. Keep both terminals open:

```sh
# terminal 1
bun run dev

# terminal 2
dotnet watch
```

Alternatively run `npm run dev`, `pnpm run dev` or `yarn run dev` in terminal 1. Open `http://localhost:5180`. You should see the template home page and a working Todos page. Click around before changing anything.

<Callout type="tip" title="Checkpoint">
If the app does not load, run `dotnet new inertia --help` and confirm the template version. The frontend must be started before `dotnet watch` reads the Vite hot file, but a refresh is enough if you started them in the other order.
</Callout>

Open these files. You do not need to understand all of them yet:

```text
Program.cs
app.html
ClientApp/app.tsx
ClientApp/Layout.tsx
ClientApp/pages/Home.tsx
ClientApp/pages/Todos/Index.tsx
```

The template already has Inertia, Vite, a deferred prop, a form and validation. We are going to grow it into a full app.

## 2. Make it look good with shadcn/ui

The template uses a tiny inline-style layout. Replace it with Tailwind and shadcn/ui.

Install the packages:

```sh
bun add -d tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
bun add class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react
```

For npm use `npm install -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite` and `npm install class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react`. For pnpm or Yarn substitute `pnpm add -D` / `pnpm add` or `yarn add -D` / `yarn add`.

Update `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
import path from 'node:path'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'
// ...your existing imports

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), inertia(), hotFile()],
  resolve: {
    alias: { '@': path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'ClientApp') },
  },
  // ...the rest stays the same
})
```

Add these two properties inside `compilerOptions` in `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./ClientApp/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Create `ClientApp/app.css` and import it from `ClientApp/app.tsx`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```

```tsx
// ClientApp/app.tsx
import './app.css'
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'

createInertiaApp()
```

Now initialize shadcn/ui from the project directory:

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn@latest init
```

For npm, pnpm or Yarn use `npx shadcn@latest init`, `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init` or `yarn dlx shadcn@latest init`. Accept the defaults. When it asks for the CSS file, choose `ClientApp/app.css`; when it asks for the import alias, use `@/`. Then add the components we need:

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn@latest add button card input label badge checkbox separator
```

For the add command use `npx shadcn@latest add ...`, `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add ...` or `yarn dlx shadcn@latest add ...` with the same component names.

<Callout type="tip" title="Checkpoint">
`ClientApp/components/ui/` should now contain `button.tsx`, `card.tsx`, `input.tsx` and the other components. If the CLI asks a question you do not understand, choose the default; you can always rerun it.
</Callout>

Replace `ClientApp/Layout.tsx` with the shared shell:

```tsx
import { Link, usePage } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { LogOut, NotebookPen, UserRound } from 'lucide-react'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { props, flash } = usePage()

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-background text-foreground">
      <header className="border-b">
        <div className="mx-auto flex h-16 max-w-5xl items-center gap-4 px-4">
          <Link href="/" className="flex items-center gap-2 font-semibold">
            <NotebookPen className="size-5 text-primary" />
            ForgetMeNot
          </Link>

          <nav className="ml-auto flex items-center gap-2">
            {props.auth ? (
              <>
                <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm"><Link href="/todos">My lists</Link></Button>
                <span className="hidden items-center gap-1 text-sm text-muted-foreground sm:flex">
                  <UserRound className="size-4" /> {props.auth.displayName}
                </span>
                <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm">
                  <Link href="/logout" method="post" as="button"><LogOut className="size-4" /> Sign out</Link>
                </Button>
              </>
            ) : (
              <>
                <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm"><Link href="/login">Sign in</Link></Button>
                <Button asChild size="sm"><Link href="/register">Create account</Link></Button>
              </>
            )}
          </nav>
        </div>
      </header>

      {flash.success && (
        <div className="border-b bg-emerald-50 px-4 py-2 text-center text-sm text-emerald-800 dark:bg-emerald-950/40 dark:text-emerald-200">
          {flash.success}
        </div>
      )}

      <main className="mx-auto max-w-5xl px-4 py-10">{children}</main>
    </div>
  )
}
```

And replace the template home page with a friendly landing page:

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Home.tsx
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { ArrowRight, CheckCircle2 } from 'lucide-react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card'
import Layout from '../Layout'

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <Layout>
      <section className="mx-auto max-w-3xl py-16 text-center">
        <Badge variant="secondary">Inertia.Net sample</Badge>
        <h1 className="mt-6 text-balance text-5xl font-semibold tracking-tight">
          Remember everything. Share what matters.
        </h1>
        <p className="mx-auto mt-4 max-w-xl text-lg text-muted-foreground">
          Private lists, public links, due dates and reminders — built with ASP.NET Core and Inertia.
        </p>
        <div className="mt-8 flex justify-center gap-3">
          <Button asChild size="lg"><Link href="/register">Create an account <ArrowRight className="size-4" /></Link></Button>
          <Button asChild size="lg" variant="outline"><Link href="/login">Sign in</Link></Button>
        </div>
      </section>

      <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
        {['Private by default', 'One public link', 'Reminders that fire once'].map((text) => (
          <Card key={text}>
            <CardContent className="flex items-center gap-2 p-5 text-sm">
              <CheckCircle2 className="size-4 text-primary" /> {text}
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        ))}
      </div>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

## 3. Give the app a clean structure

The template keeps everything in `Program.cs`. We will move the setup into small files so `Program.cs` stays readable. Create these folders:

```text
ForgetMeNot/
  Data/
  Endpoints/
  Infrastructure/
```

The final `Program.cs` is only a few lines:

```csharp
using ForgetMeNot;
using ForgetMeNot.Endpoints;
using ForgetMeNot.Infrastructure;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.AddForgetMeNot();

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseForgetMeNot();
app.MapForgetMeNot();

app.Run();
```

Each extension does one job:

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Infrastructure/ForgetMeNotSetup.cs` | The one `AddForgetMeNot()` and `UseForgetMeNot()` entry point |
| `Infrastructure/DataSetup.cs` | EF Core and SQLite |
| `Infrastructure/SessionAuthSetup.cs` | Session, antiforgery and password hashing |
| `Infrastructure/InertiaSetup.cs` | Inertia options, shared props and SSR |
| `Infrastructure/SessionAuth.cs` | Sign in/out helpers and the `RequireSessionUser` filter |
| `Endpoints/AuthEndpoints.cs` | Register, login and logout |
| `Endpoints/TodoEndpoints.cs` | Private lists and items |
| `Endpoints/PublicEndpoints.cs` | The public share page |

A beginner can read `Program.cs` in one glance. That is the point.

The route table is also one readable file:

```csharp
// Endpoints/ForgetMeNotEndpoints.cs
public static class ForgetMeNotEndpoints
{
    public static IEndpointRouteBuilder MapForgetMeNot(this IEndpointRouteBuilder app)
    {
        app.MapGet("/health", () => Results.Ok("ok"));
        app.MapGet("/", () => Render("Home"));
        app.MapGet("/login", () => Render("Auth/Login"));
        app.MapGet("/register", () => Render("Auth/Register"));

        app.MapAuthEndpoints();
        app.MapTodoEndpoints();
        app.MapPublicEndpoints();
        return app;
    }
}
```

If a route is hard to find, start there.

## 4. Model the data

Add the entities:

```csharp
// Data/Entities.cs
public sealed class AppUser
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public required string Email { get; set; }
    public required string DisplayName { get; set; }
    public required string PasswordHash { get; set; }
    public List<TodoList> Lists { get; } = [];
}

public sealed class TodoList
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public int UserId { get; set; }
    public AppUser User { get; set; } = null!;
    public required string Title { get; set; }
    public required string PublicSlug { get; set; }
    public bool IsPublic { get; set; }
    public List<TodoItem> Items { get; } = [];
}

public sealed class TodoItem
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public int TodoListId { get; set; }
    public TodoList List { get; set; } = null!;
    public required string Title { get; set; }
    public bool IsDone { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? DueAt { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? RemindAt { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? RemindedAt { get; set; }
}
```

`PublicSlug` is the secret part of a public URL. `RemindedAt` makes reminder delivery idempotent: if the worker restarts, it does not send the same reminder again.

```csharp
// Data/AppDbContext.cs
public sealed class AppDbContext(DbContextOptions<AppDbContext> options) : DbContext(options)
{
    public DbSet<AppUser> Users => Set<AppUser>();
    public DbSet<TodoList> Lists => Set<TodoList>();
    public DbSet<TodoItem> Items => Set<TodoItem>();

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder model)
    {
        model.Entity<TodoList>().HasIndex(l => l.PublicSlug).IsUnique();
        model.Entity<TodoItem>().HasIndex(i => new { i.TodoListId, i.RemindAt, i.RemindedAt });
    }
}
```

```csharp
// Data/PageModels.cs
public sealed record TodoListDto(int Id, string Title, string PublicSlug, bool IsPublic, int Total, int Open);
public sealed record TodoItemDto(int Id, string Title, bool IsDone, DateTimeOffset? DueAt);
public sealed record TodoListHeader(int Id, string Title, string PublicSlug, bool IsPublic);
public sealed record ReminderDto(int Id, string Title, DateTimeOffset RemindAt);
public sealed record TodoStats(int Open, int Done, int DueToday);
public sealed record PublicListHeader(int Id, string Title, string Owner, int OpenCount);
public sealed record PublicTodoDto(int Id, string Title, DateTimeOffset? DueAt);
public sealed record TodoItemsPage(List<TodoItemDto> Data);
public sealed record PublicTodoPage(List<PublicTodoDto> Data);

public sealed class CreateListForm
{
    [Required, MaxLength(120)]
    public string? Title { get; set; }

    public bool IsPublic { get; set; }
}

public sealed class CreateTodoForm
{
    [Required, MaxLength(200)]
    public string? Title { get; set; }

    public DateTimeOffset? DueAt { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? RemindAt { get; set; }
}
```

The template uses source-generated JSON. Add every prop and form type to its `AppJsonContext`:

```csharp
[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(AuthUser))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(SharedProps))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Flash))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(TodoListDto))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<TodoListDto>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(TodoItemDto))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(TodoListHeader))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(TodoItemsPage))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(ReminderDto))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<ReminderDto>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(TodoStats))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(PublicListHeader))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(PublicTodoDto))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(PublicTodoPage))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(RegisterForm))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(LoginForm))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(CreateListForm))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(CreateTodoForm))]
internal sealed partial class AppJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;
```

The data setup extension:

```csharp
// Infrastructure/DataSetup.cs
public static class DataSetup
{
    public static WebApplicationBuilder AddForgetMeNotData(this WebApplicationBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o =>
            o.UseSqlite("Data Source=forgetmenot.db"));
        return builder;
    }

    public static WebApplication EnsureForgetMeNotData(this WebApplication app)
    {
        using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
        scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<AppDbContext>().Database.EnsureCreated();
        return app;
    }
}
```

`EnsureCreated()` is perfect for a first app. For production, replace it with EF migrations.

## 5. Use sessions for sign-in

Sessions keep the signed-in user id and Inertia's flash/error state on the server. The browser only holds an HttpOnly session cookie.

```csharp
// Infrastructure/SessionAuthSetup.cs
public static class SessionAuthSetup
{
    public static WebApplicationBuilder AddForgetMeNotSessionAuth(this WebApplicationBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.Services.AddDistributedMemoryCache();
        builder.Services.AddSession(o =>
        {
            o.Cookie.Name = ".fmn.session";
            o.Cookie.HttpOnly = true;
            o.Cookie.IsEssential = true;
            o.Cookie.SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax;
            o.Cookie.SecurePolicy = builder.Environment.IsDevelopment()
                ? CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest
                : CookieSecurePolicy.Always;
            o.IdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromDays(7);
        });

        builder.Services.AddAntiforgery(o => o.HeaderName = InertiaHeaders.XsrfToken);
        builder.Services.AddScoped<IPasswordHasher<AppUser>, PasswordHasher<AppUser>>();
        return builder;
    }

    public static WebApplication UseForgetMeNotSession(this WebApplication app)
    {
        app.UseSession();
        return app;
    }
}
```

The session helpers and the endpoint filter:

```csharp
// Infrastructure/SessionAuth.cs
public static class SessionAuth
{
    public const string UserIdKey = "fmn.user-id";
    public const string DisplayNameKey = "fmn.display-name";

    public static int? UserId(this HttpContext http) => http.Session.GetInt32(UserIdKey);

    public static void SignIn(this HttpContext http, AppUser user)
    {
        http.Session.SetInt32(UserIdKey, user.Id);
        http.Session.SetString(DisplayNameKey, user.DisplayName);
    }

    public static void SignOut(this HttpContext http) => http.Session.Clear();
}

public sealed class RequireSessionUser : IEndpointFilter
{
    public async ValueTask<object?> InvokeAsync(
        EndpointFilterInvocationContext context,
        EndpointFilterDelegate next)
    {
        if (context.HttpContext.UserId() is null)
        {
            return Inertia.Net.Inertia.Location("/login");
        }

        return await next(context);
    }
}
```

<Callout type="warning" title="One instance for this sample">
`AddDistributedMemoryCache()` keeps sessions in memory. That is fine for one app instance. For more than one replica, register a shared cache such as Redis, or the session will only exist on the instance that created it.
</Callout>

## 6. Hide the Inertia setup

`InertiaSetup.cs` is the only file a beginner needs to know when they want to change Inertia behavior.

```csharp
// Infrastructure/InertiaSetup.cs
public static class InertiaSetup
{
    public static WebApplicationBuilder AddForgetMeNotInertia(this WebApplicationBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
        {
            o.Share("appName", "ForgetMeNot");
            o.Share("auth", ctx =>
            {
                var id = ctx.Session.GetInt32(SessionAuth.UserIdKey);
                var name = ctx.Session.GetString(SessionAuth.DisplayNameKey);
                return id is null ? null : new AuthUser(id.Value, name ?? "You");
            });
            o.Share("baseUrl", ctx =>
                $"{ctx.Request.Scheme}://{ctx.Request.Host}{ctx.Request.PathBase}");

            o.Pages.Directory = "ClientApp/pages";
            o.Vite.Prefetch = VitePrefetch.Waterfall;
            o.State.UseSession();                  // flash/errors live in the session too
            o.TypeScript.OutputPath = "ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts";
            o.TypeScript.SharedProps<SharedProps>().FlashData<Flash>();
            o.Ssr.BundlePath = "ssr/ssr.js";
            o.Ssr.Mode = SsrMode.Preferred;
            o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n => n.Executable = "bun");
        });

        builder.Services.AddInertiaDevTools();
        return builder;
    }

    public static WebApplication UseForgetMeNotInertia(this WebApplication app)
    {
        app.UseInertia();
        app.UseInertiaAntiforgery();
        return app;
    }
}

public sealed record AuthUser(int Id, string DisplayName);
public sealed record SharedProps(string AppName, AuthUser? Auth, string BaseUrl);
public sealed record Flash(string? Success);
```

Now the aggregate setup:

```csharp
// Infrastructure/ForgetMeNotSetup.cs
public static class ForgetMeNotSetup
{
    public static WebApplicationBuilder AddForgetMeNot(this WebApplicationBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(o =>
        {
            o.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
            o.ForwardLimit = 1;
            o.KnownIPNetworks.Clear();
            o.KnownProxies.Clear();
        });

        builder.Services.AddValidation();
        builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
        builder.Services.AddResponseCompression(o => o.EnableForHttps = true);
        builder.Services.ConfigureHttpJsonOptions(o =>
            o.SerializerOptions.TypeInfoResolverChain.Insert(0, AppJsonContext.Default));

        builder.AddForgetMeNotData();
        builder.AddForgetMeNotSessionAuth();
        builder.AddForgetMeNotInertia();
        return builder;
    }

    public static WebApplication UseForgetMeNot(this WebApplication app)
    {
        app.UseForwardedHeaders();
        app.UseResponseCompression();
        app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
        {
            OnPrepareResponse = c =>
            {
                if (c.Context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/build/assets"))
                    c.Context.Response.Headers.CacheControl = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
            },
        });

        app.UseForgetMeNotSession();
        app.UseForgetMeNotInertia();
        app.EnsureForgetMeNotData();
        return app;
    }
}
```

`UseSession()` must run before `UseInertia()`. Add forwarded-header configuration if you deploy behind Coolify or another TLS proxy.

## 7. Register, sign in and sign out

The endpoints live in `Endpoints/AuthEndpoints.cs` and are mapped from `MapForgetMeNot()`. `WithInertiaValidation()` turns model errors into a redirect back with `errors`.

```csharp
public sealed class RegisterForm
{
    [Required, EmailAddress]
    public string? Email { get; set; }

    [Required, MinLength(8)]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    [Required, MaxLength(80)]
    public string? DisplayName { get; set; }
}

public sealed class LoginForm
{
    [Required, EmailAddress]
    public string? Email { get; set; }

    [Required]
    public string? Password { get; set; }
}

public static class AuthEndpoints
{
    public static IEndpointRouteBuilder MapAuthEndpoints(this IEndpointRouteBuilder app)
    {
        app.MapPost("/register", async (
            RegisterForm form, AppDbContext db, IPasswordHasher<AppUser> hasher, HttpContext http) =>
        {
            var email = form.Email!.Trim().ToLowerInvariant();
            if (await db.Users.AnyAsync(u => u.Email == email))
            {
                return Back().WithErrors(new Dictionary<string, string>
                {
                    ["email"] = "An account with this email already exists.",
                });
            }

            var user = new AppUser
            {
                Email = email,
                DisplayName = form.DisplayName!.Trim(),
                PasswordHash = "",
            };
            user.PasswordHash = hasher.HashPassword(user, form.Password!);

            db.Users.Add(user);
            await db.SaveChangesAsync();

            http.Inertia().Flash("success", "Account created. Sign in to continue.");
            return Results.Redirect("/login");
        }).WithInertiaValidation();

        app.MapPost("/login", async (
            LoginForm form, AppDbContext db, IPasswordHasher<AppUser> hasher, HttpContext http) =>
        {
            var email = form.Email!.Trim().ToLowerInvariant();
            var user = await db.Users.SingleOrDefaultAsync(u => u.Email == email);

            if (user is null || hasher.VerifyHashedPassword(user, user.PasswordHash, form.Password!)
                == PasswordVerificationResult.Failed)
            {
                return Back().WithErrors(new Dictionary<string, string>
                {
                    ["email"] = "These credentials do not match our records.",
                });
            }

            http.SignIn(user);
            return Results.Redirect("/todos");
        }).WithInertiaValidation();

        app.MapPost("/logout", (HttpContext http) =>
        {
            http.SignOut();
            http.Inertia().ClearHistory();
            return Results.Redirect("/");
        });

        return app;
    }
}
```

The login page uses `useForm` and shadcn components:

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Auth/Login.tsx
import { Link, useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import type { FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'
import Layout from '../../Layout'

export default function Login() {
  const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '' })

  const submit = (event: FormEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    form.post('/login', { onFinish: () => form.reset('password') })
  }

  return (
    <Layout>
      <Card className="mx-auto mt-12 max-w-md">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Welcome back</CardTitle>
          <CardDescription>Sign in to see your lists and reminders.</CardDescription>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <form onSubmit={submit} className="space-y-4">
            <div className="space-y-2">
              <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
              <Input id="email" type="email" value={form.data.email} onChange={(e) => form.setData('email', e.target.value)} />
              {form.errors.email && <p className="text-sm text-red-600">{form.errors.email}</p>}
            </div>

            <div className="space-y-2">
              <Label htmlFor="password">Password</Label>
              <Input id="password" type="password" value={form.data.password} onChange={(e) => form.setData('password', e.target.value)} />
              {form.errors.password && <p className="text-sm text-red-600">{form.errors.password}</p>}
            </div>

            <Button type="submit" className="w-full" disabled={form.processing}>
              {form.processing ? 'Signing in...' : 'Sign in'}
            </Button>

            <p className="text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              New here? <Link href="/register" className="font-medium text-foreground underline">Create an account</Link>
            </p>
          </form>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

The register page is the same pattern with `displayName`, `email` and `password`.

<Callout type="tip" title="Checkpoint">
Create an account, sign in, refresh the page and confirm you stay signed in. Sign out and confirm you return to the home page. If the session cookie is not sent, check that `UseForgetMeNotSession()` runs before `UseForgetMeNotInertia()`.
</Callout>

## 8. Build the dashboard

Map the private endpoints from `TodoEndpoints.cs`:

```csharp
public static class TodoEndpoints
{
    public static IEndpointRouteBuilder MapTodoEndpoints(this IEndpointRouteBuilder app)
    {
        app.MapGet("/todos", async (HttpContext http, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) =>
        {
            var userId = http.UserId()!.Value;

            var lists = await db.Lists
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(l => l.UserId == userId)
                .OrderBy(l => l.Title)
                .Select(l => new TodoListDto(
                    l.Id, l.Title, l.PublicSlug, l.IsPublic,
                    l.Items.Count, l.Items.Count(i => !i.IsDone)))
                .ToListAsync(ct);

            return Render("Todos/Index", new InertiaProps
            {
                ["lists"] = lists,
                ["reminders"] = Defer(ct => LoadReminders(db, userId, ct), group: "sidebar"),
                ["stats"] = Defer(ct => LoadStats(db, userId, ct), group: "sidebar"),
            });
        }).AddEndpointFilter<RequireSessionUser>();

        // ...the list, create and toggle endpoints below...
        return app;
    }
}
```

Create a list from the dashboard:

```csharp
app.MapPost("/lists", async (
    CreateListForm form, HttpContext http, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var list = new TodoList
    {
        UserId = http.UserId()!.Value,
        Title = form.Title!.Trim(),
        IsPublic = form.IsPublic,
        PublicSlug = NewPublicSlug(),
    };
    db.Lists.Add(list);
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    return Results.Redirect($"/todos/{list.Id}");
}).AddEndpointFilter<RequireSessionUser>().WithInertiaValidation();

static string NewPublicSlug() =>
    Convert.ToHexString(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(8)).ToLowerInvariant();
```

The two deferred loaders:

```csharp
static async Task<List<ReminderDto>> LoadReminders(AppDbContext db, int userId, CancellationToken ct) =>
    await db.Items
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(i => i.List.UserId == userId && i.RemindAt != null && i.RemindedAt == null)
        .OrderBy(i => i.RemindAt)
        .Take(10)
        .Select(i => new ReminderDto(i.Id, i.Title, i.RemindAt!.Value))
        .ToListAsync(ct);

static async Task<TodoStats> LoadStats(AppDbContext db, int userId, CancellationToken ct)
{
    var today = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Date;
    return new TodoStats(
        await db.Items.CountAsync(i => i.List.UserId == userId && !i.IsDone, ct),
        await db.Items.CountAsync(i => i.List.UserId == userId && i.IsDone, ct),
        await db.Items.CountAsync(i => i.List.UserId == userId && !i.IsDone
            && i.DueAt != null && i.DueAt < today.AddDays(1), ct));
}
```

The dashboard React page uses `Card`, `Badge` and `Deferred`:

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Todos/Index.tsx
import { Deferred, Link, useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import Layout from '../../Layout'

interface Props {
  lists: { id: number; title: string; isPublic: boolean; total: number; open: number }[]
  reminders?: { id: number; title: string; remindAt: string }[]
  stats?: { open: number; done: number; dueToday: number }
}

export default function Index({ lists, reminders, stats }: Props) {
  const form = useForm({ title: '' })

  return (
    <Layout>
      <div className="flex items-end justify-between gap-4">
        <div>
          <h1 className="text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight">Your lists</h1>
          <p className="mt-1 text-muted-foreground">Private by default. Share a list when you want to.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="mt-8 grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
        {lists.map((list) => (
          <Link key={list.id} href={`/todos/${list.id}`}>
            <Card className="transition-colors hover:border-primary/40">
              <CardHeader>
                <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
                  <CardTitle>{list.title}</CardTitle>
                  <Badge variant={list.isPublic ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>{list.isPublic ? 'Public' : 'Private'}</Badge>
                </div>
              </CardHeader>
              <CardContent className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
                {list.open} open of {list.total}
              </CardContent>
            </Card>
          </Link>
        ))}
      </div>

      <Card className="mt-8">
        <CardHeader><CardTitle>New list</CardTitle></CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <form onSubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); form.post('/lists', { onSuccess: () => form.reset() }) }} className="flex gap-2">
            <Input value={form.data.title} onChange={(e) => form.setData('title', e.target.value)} placeholder="Weekend plans" />
            <Button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}><Plus className="size-4" /> Add</Button>
          </form>
          {form.errors.title && <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-red-600">{form.errors.title}</p>}
        </CardContent>
      </Card>

      <div className="mt-8 grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
        <Deferred data="stats" fallback={<p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Counting...</p>}>
          <Card>
            <CardHeader><CardTitle>Overview</CardTitle></CardHeader>
            <CardContent className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              {stats?.open} open · {stats?.done} done · {stats?.dueToday} due today
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        </Deferred>

        <Deferred data="reminders" fallback={<p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Loading reminders...</p>}>
          <Card>
            <CardHeader><CardTitle>Upcoming reminders</CardTitle></CardHeader>
            <CardContent>
              {reminders?.length ? reminders.map((reminder) => (
                <p key={reminder.id} className="text-sm">{reminder.title}</p>
              )) : <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Nothing scheduled.</p>}
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        </Deferred>
      </div>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

## 9. Load items in pages

These snippets live inside `MapTodoEndpoints` in `Endpoints/TodoEndpoints.cs`.

Add the list endpoint with `Scroll`:

```csharp
app.MapGet("/todos/{id:int}", async (
    int id, int? page, HttpContext http, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var userId = http.UserId()!.Value;
    var list = await db.Lists
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(l => l.Id == id && l.UserId == userId)
        .Select(l => new TodoListHeader(l.Id, l.Title, l.PublicSlug, l.IsPublic))
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct);

    if (list is null) return Results.NotFound();

    const int pageSize = 40;
    var current = Math.Max(1, page ?? 1);
    var rows = await db.Items
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(i => i.TodoListId == id)
        .OrderBy(i => i.IsDone)
        .ThenBy(i => i.DueAt)
        .ThenBy(i => i.Id)
        .Skip((current - 1) * pageSize)
        .Take(pageSize + 1)
        .Select(i => new TodoItemDto(i.Id, i.Title, i.IsDone, i.DueAt))
        .ToListAsync(ct);

    return Render("Todos/Show", new InertiaProps
    {
        ["list"] = list,
        ["items"] = Scroll(
            new TodoItemsPage(rows.Take(pageSize).ToList()),
            metadata: ScrollMetadata.FromPage(current, rows.Count > pageSize)),
    });
}).AddEndpointFilter<RequireSessionUser>();
```

The React page asks for the next page as the user scrolls:

Add the write endpoints:

```csharp
app.MapPost("/todos/{id:int}/items", async (
    int id, CreateTodoForm form, HttpContext http, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var userId = http.UserId()!.Value;
    if (!await db.Lists.AnyAsync(l => l.Id == id && l.UserId == userId, ct))
        return Results.NotFound();

    db.Items.Add(new TodoItem
    {
        TodoListId = id,
        Title = form.Title!.Trim(),
        DueAt = form.DueAt,
        RemindAt = form.RemindAt,
    });
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);

    return Back().WithFlash("success", "Todo added");
}).AddEndpointFilter<RequireSessionUser>().WithInertiaValidation();

app.MapPatch("/items/{id:int}", async (
    int id, HttpContext http, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var userId = http.UserId()!.Value;
    var item = await db.Items
        .Include(i => i.List)
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(i => i.Id == id && i.List.UserId == userId, ct);

    if (item is null) return Results.NotFound();

    item.IsDone = !item.IsDone;
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    return Back();
}).AddEndpointFilter<RequireSessionUser>();
```

The React page asks for the next page as the user scrolls:

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Todos/Show.tsx
import { InfiniteScroll, router, useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import type { FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import Layout from '../../Layout'

interface Props {
  list: { id: number; title: string }
  items: { data: { id: number; title: string; isDone: boolean; dueAt: string | null }[] }
}

export default function Show({ list, items }: Props) {
  const form = useForm({ title: '', dueAt: '', remindAt: '' })

  const submit = (event: FormEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    form.post(`/todos/${list.id}/items`, { onSuccess: () => form.reset() })
  }

  return (
    <Layout>
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{list.title}</h1>
      <p className="mt-1 text-muted-foreground">Loaded in pages, merged as you scroll.</p>

      <Card className="mt-6">
        <CardContent className="p-4">
          <form onSubmit={submit} className="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-[1fr_auto_auto_auto]">
            <Input placeholder="What needs doing?" value={form.data.title} onChange={(e) => form.setData('title', e.target.value)} />
            <Input type="datetime-local" value={form.data.dueAt} onChange={(e) => form.setData('dueAt', e.target.value)} aria-label="Due date" />
            <Input type="datetime-local" value={form.data.remindAt} onChange={(e) => form.setData('remindAt', e.target.value)} aria-label="Remind me" />
            <Button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}>Add</Button>
          </form>
          {form.errors.title && <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-red-600">{form.errors.title}</p>}
        </CardContent>
      </Card>

      <InfiniteScroll data="items" className="mt-8 space-y-3">
        {items.data.map((item) => (
          <Card key={item.id}>
            <CardContent className="flex items-center gap-3 p-4">
              <Checkbox checked={item.isDone} onCheckedChange={() => router.patch(`/items/${item.id}`)} />
              <span className={item.isDone ? 'text-muted-foreground line-through' : ''}>{item.title}</span>
              {item.dueAt && <span className="ml-auto text-xs text-muted-foreground">{new Date(item.dueAt).toLocaleDateString()}</span>}
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        ))}
      </InfiniteScroll>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

`Scroll` merges the `data` array and tells `InfiniteScroll` which URL parameter to use. The browser only renders the pages it has requested.

<Callout type="tip" title="Checkpoint">
Create a list, add more than one page of items, then scroll. The network panel should show a partial reload for each new page, and existing items should remain in place.
</Callout>

## 10. Share a list publicly

Public routes do not use `RequireSessionUser`. Use a random slug, not the numeric id, and return a small DTO instead of the entity.

```csharp
app.MapGet("/p/{slug}", async (
    string slug, int? page, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var list = await db.Lists
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(l => l.PublicSlug == slug && l.IsPublic)
        .Select(l => new PublicListHeader(l.Id, l.Title, l.User.DisplayName, l.Items.Count(i => !i.IsDone)))
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct);

    if (list is null) return Results.NotFound();

    const int pageSize = 25;
    var current = Math.Max(1, page ?? 1);
    var rows = await db.Items
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(i => i.TodoListId == list.Id && !i.IsDone)
        .OrderBy(i => i.DueAt)
        .ThenBy(i => i.Id)
        .Skip((current - 1) * pageSize)
        .Take(pageSize + 1)
        .Select(i => new PublicTodoDto(i.Id, i.Title, i.DueAt))
        .ToListAsync(ct);
```
