```csharp
    return Render("Public/Show", new InertiaProps
    {
        ["list"] = list,
        ["items"] = Scroll(
            new PublicTodoPage(rows.Take(pageSize).ToList()),
            metadata: ScrollMetadata.FromPage(current, rows.Count > pageSize)),
    });
});
```

The handler above is the body of `PublicEndpoints.MapPublicEndpoints` in `Endpoints/PublicEndpoints.cs`.

```csharp
static string NewPublicSlug() =>
    Convert.ToHexString(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(8)).ToLowerInvariant();
```

The public page is the same `InfiniteScroll` pattern, wrapped in a clean card:

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Public/Show.tsx
import { InfiniteScroll } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import Layout from '../../Layout'

interface Props {
  list: { title: string; owner: string; openCount: number }
  items: { data: { id: number; title: string; dueAt: string | null }[] }
}

export default function PublicShow({ list, items }: Props) {
  return (
    <Layout>
      <Badge variant="secondary">Public list</Badge>
      <h1 className="mt-4 text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{list.title}</h1>
      <p className="mt-2 text-muted-foreground">Shared by {list.owner} · {list.openCount} open items</p>

      <InfiniteScroll data="items" className="mt-8 space-y-3">

            <CardHeader><CardTitle className="text-base">{item.title}</CardTitle></CardHeader>
            {item.dueAt && <CardContent className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Due {new Date(item.dueAt).toLocaleDateString()}</CardContent>}
          </Card>
        ))}
      </InfiniteScroll>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

Put the `/p/{slug}` handler in `Endpoints/PublicEndpoints.cs` inside `MapPublicEndpoints`, then add it to the route table. Open the URL in a private browser window to prove no session is needed.

<Callout type="warning" title="Do not leak the private shape">
Return `PublicTodoDto`, not `TodoItem`. Public pages must not include `RemindAt`, the owner's email or private lists.
</Callout>

## 11. Send reminders once

A background service checks for due items every minute, sends them, and records `RemindedAt`.

```csharp
public interface IEmailSender
{
    Task SendAsync(string to, string subject, string body, CancellationToken ct = default);
}

public sealed class ReminderWorker(
    IServiceScopeFactory scopes,
    ILogger<ReminderWorker> logger) : BackgroundService
{
    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1));

        while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))
        {
            using var scope = scopes.CreateScope();
            var db = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<AppDbContext>();
            var mail = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IEmailSender>();
            var now = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;

            var due = await db.Items
                .Include(i => i.List).ThenInclude(l => l.User)
                .Where(i => i.RemindAt != null && i.RemindAt <= now && i.RemindedAt == null)
                .OrderBy(i => i.RemindAt)
                .Take(100)
                .ToListAsync(stoppingToken);

            foreach (var item in due)
            {
                await mail.SendAsync(item.List.User.Email, $"Reminder: {item.Title}", item.Title, stoppingToken);
                item.RemindedAt = now;
            }

            if (due.Count > 0)
            {
                await db.SaveChangesAsync(stoppingToken);
                logger.LogInformation("Sent {Count} reminders", due.Count);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Register the service in `ForgetMeNotSetup`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddScoped<IEmailSender, SmtpEmailSender>(); // your implementation
builder.Services.AddHostedService<ReminderWorker>();
```

For a single instance, the timer is enough. For several instances, use a durable queue with leases (TickerQ, Hangfire or a database outbox) so only one worker claims each reminder.

## 12. Test the important paths

Add `public partial class Program;` to the app, then use `Inertia.Net.Testing`:

```csharp
var page = await client.GetInertiaPageAsync("/todos");

new AssertableInertia(page)
    .Component("Todos/Index")
    .Has("lists")
    .Missing("reminders");

var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(client, "sidebar");
new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("reminders");
```

For the public route, sign out first and assert that `remindAt` and the owner's email are absent. This is the test that protects you from accidentally returning the entity.

## 13. Run it in production

Build both bundles with your package manager:

```sh
bun run build
dotnet publish -c Release
```

Use `npm run build`, `pnpm run build` or `yarn run build` instead if preferred. ForgetMeNot starts `ssr/ssr.js` with Bun; install Bun in the production environment or configure a compatible Node runtime. The container pattern is in the docs app and the published samples:

- `Dockerfile` from `docs/Inertia.Net.Docs`
- `samples/Inkwell/Dockerfile` for a single app with SQLite and Bun SSR
- `samples/CarParker/Dockerfile` for a Mongo-backed app with public pages
- `samples/TechLandierDistributed/Dockerfile` for a separate SSR pool

Read [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering) and [Deploying behind a proxy](/docs/deploying) before exposing the app publicly. Size the container with the [memory table](/docs/performance#memory-and-hosting).
